title: Government's Plans in Our Continuing Fight Against COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Government's Plans in Our Continuing Fight Against COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: Global COVID-19 cases and deaths
sections.summary: Globally, there were about 1.1 million cases and 62,000 deaths at that time, and over 5,000,000 infections and over 340,000 deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At that time, there were about 1.1 million cases and 62,000 deaths due to COVID-19 globally.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Globally, over 5,000,000 people have been infected and over 340,000 lives have been lost.

sections.label: US April unemployment rate
sections.summary: In the US, the unemployment rate for April increased to 14.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the US, the unemployment rates for April has increased to 14.7%.

sections.label: Singapore GDP growth forecast downgrade
sections.summary: MTI downgraded Singapore's GDP growth forecast from -4% to -1% to -7% to -4%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our economy has been deeply impacted by the global shocks.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This morning, the Ministry of Trade and Industry further downgraded Singapore's GDP growth forecast from -4% to -1% to -7% to -4%.

sections.label: Resident unemployment rate March 2020
sections.summary: The resident unemployment rate rose to 3.3% in March 2020, the highest since December 2009.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Based on preliminary estimates, the resident unemployment rate rose to 3.3% in March 2020 – the highest since December 2009.

sections.label: Budgets and Jobs Support Scheme funding
sections.summary: Close to $100 billion, almost 20% of GDP, is dedicated with the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, including $3.8 billion for measures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Together with the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, we are dedicating close to $100 billion to support our people in this battle, which is almost 20% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Part of this Supplementary Budget also provides $3.8 billion for the measures, including the enhancements to the Jobs Support Scheme announced on 21 April 2020 for the extended circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme enhancements
sections.summary: Three enhancements to the JSS are made, the first increasing payout duration by one month for all firms.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Coming out of the circuit breaker, businesses will not be able to return immediately to pre-circuit breaker levels of operations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, I reviewed the original JSS schedule with fellow Ministers and will make three enhancements to the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The first enhancement is to increase the duration of JSS payouts by one month for all firms.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I previously announced that the JSS would cover nine months, computed based on wages paid to local employees up to July 2020.

sections.label: Wage support for impacted sectors
sections.summary: Wage support for more severely impacted sectors rises from 25% to 75% or 50%, with retail and marine and offshore receiving 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This arose from feedback from industry associations and businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will increase the level of wage support for firms in sectors that are more severely impacted, from the previous 25%, to either 75% or 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Firms in the retail, and marine and offshore sectors will now receive 50% support.

sections.label: JSS enhancements cost and payouts
sections.summary: Three JSS enhancements cost $2.9 billion, and the JSS flows $23.5 billion to firms for 10 months of wage costs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, these three enhancements to the JSS will cost $2.9 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Through the JSS, we are flowing a total of $23.5 billion to firms to support wage costs for 10 months.

sections.label: CPF increase for senior workers deferred
sections.summary: The Government will defer the planned CPF contribution rate increase for senior workers by one year, to 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help businesses manage costs in these challenging times, the Government will defer the planned increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers by one year, from 1 January 2021 to 1 January 2022.

sections.label: Rental relief for SME tenants
sections.summary: If the Bill passes, SME tenants in commercial properties with significant revenue drop get four months of rental relief, shared equally by Government and landlords.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: If the Bill is passed by Parliament, SME tenants in commercial properties who have suffered a significant revenue drop will benefit from a total of four months of rental relief – shared equally between the Government and landlords.

sections.label: Funding for start-ups and sectors
sections.summary: It sets aside $285 million to match at least $285 million in private investments, in addition to $300 million for deep-tech start-ups under Startup SG Equity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will help them sustain their innovation and entrepreneurship journey.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $285 million, to catalyse and crowd in at least another $285 million in matching private investments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is in addition to the $300 million I had set aside under the Unity Budget for deep-tech start-ups to gain better access to capital, expertise and industry networks under Startup SG Equity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Government agencies have also been rolling out support packages to address other sector-specific needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have introduced packages for the aviation, tourism, land transport, arts and culture, financial and maritime sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will introduce further support for the built environment sector, which includes construction.

sections.label: Business re-opening by July
sections.summary: Based on current re-opening plans, most businesses are expected to re-open by July.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Based on our current re-opening plans, we expect most businesses to re-open by July.

sections.label: Funding for business digital transformation
sections.summary: More than $500 million is allocated to support businesses in their digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To accelerate change, I will allocate more than $500 million to support businesses in their digital transformation.

sections.label: Bonus for e-payment adoption
sections.summary: IMDA, NEA, JTC, HDB and Enterprise Singapore will provide a $300 monthly bonus over five months to encourage stallholders to use e-payments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: IMDA, NEA, JTC, HDB and Enterprise Singapore will provide a bonus of $300 per month over five months to encourage more stallholders in hawker centres, wet markets, coffee shops, and industrial canteens to use e-payments and avoid having to handle cash.

sections.label: Digital Resilience Bonus payouts
sections.summary: A Digital Resilience Bonus offers eligible businesses up to $5,000 for adopting PayNow Corporate, e-invoicing, and business process or e-commerce solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To give a further boost, we will introduce a Digital Resilience Bonus to help businesses take their next step to digitalise.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Eligible businesses can receive a payout of up to $5,000 if they adopt PayNow Corporate and e-invoicing, as well as business process or e-commerce solutions.

sections.label: Bonus tier and digitalisation funding
sections.summary: The Digital Resilience Bonus has an extra $5,000 tier for F&B and retail businesses, and $250 million is set aside for digitalisation partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Digital Resilience Bonus will have an additional tier of $5,000 for F&B and retail businesses which also incorporate advanced solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also set aside $250 million to help businesses digitalise in partnership with platform solution providers and industry champions.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: The Budget launches an SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package creating close to 100,000 opportunities: 40,000 jobs, 25,000 traineeships and 30,000 skills training.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Budget, I will launch an SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, to create close to 100,000 opportunities in three areas – 40,000 jobs, 25,000 traineeships and 30,000 skills training.

sections.label: Jobs component of SGUnited package
sections.summary: The jobs component expands public and private sector job opportunities to more than 40,000, with the public sector creating 15,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The first component in this SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package is jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will continue to expand the number of job opportunities, in both the public and private sectors, to more than 40,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Together with jobs to meet short-term needs related to COVID-19 operations, such as healthcare declaration assistants and swabbers, the public sector will create 15,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our agencies will also work with businesses to create 25,000 jobs.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships programme places
sections.summary: 21,000 places come from the SGUnited Traineeships programme and 4,000 from a new SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeships scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Of this, 21,000 will be from the SGUnited Traineeships programme, and another 4,000 places from a new SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeships scheme.

sections.label: SGUnited Skills programme training capacity
sections.summary: A new SGUnited Skills programme expands training capacity for about 30,000 jobseekers this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The third component in the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package is a new SGUnited Skills programme to expand training capacity for about 30,000 jobseekers this year.

sections.label: Career guidance and training allowance
sections.summary: Participants receive career guidance, job placement support and a $1,200 monthly training allowance during training.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: They will also be provided with career guidance and job placement support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: They will also receive a training allowance of $1,200 per month during the course of their training.

sections.label: Incentive for workers aged 40 and above
sections.summary: For eligible workers aged 40 and above, the incentive doubles to cover 40% of salary over six months, capped at $12,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For eligible workers aged 40 and above, I will double the incentive to cover 40% of their salary over six months, capped at $12,000 in total.

sections.label: Incentive for workers under 40
sections.summary: For eligible workers under 40, the incentive covers 20% of monthly salary over six months, capped at $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For eligible workers under 40, this incentive will cover 20% of their monthly salary over six months, capped at $6,000 in total.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills package funding
sections.summary: About $2 billion is set aside this year for the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package to strengthen employment and training support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, to deal with the impact of COVID-19 on jobs, I will set aside about $2 billion for the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package this year to strengthen employment and training support for our workers.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant top-up
sections.summary: An additional $800 million is set aside for the COVID-19 Support Grant, with over 100,000 self-employed persons receiving a first $3,000 payout this week.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To strengthen support for our families, I will set aside another $800 million for the COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over 100,000 self-employed persons will be receiving their first payout of $3,000 this week.

sections.label: Solidarity Utilities Credit for households
sections.summary: A one-off $100 Solidarity Utilities Credit is provided to each household with at least one Singapore Citizen.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To thank all Singaporeans for doing our part in staying home for Singapore, I will provide a one-off $100 Solidarity Utilities Credit to each household with at least one Singapore Citizen.

sections.label: MOE devices and digital learning
sections.summary: MOE loaned over 22,000 computing devices and internet dongles and will accelerate the timeline for all Secondary School students to own a digital learning device.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support students from lower-income families who may not have digital access at home, MOE loaned over 22,000 computing devices and internet dongles to enable all students to benefit from full home-based learning and continue to connect with their teachers and friends.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As part of longer term plans to support digital literacy for all students, MOE will accelerate the timeline for all Secondary School students to own a digital learning device.

sections.label: Tote Board charity matching top-up
sections.summary: The Government will partner the Tote Board to enhance donation matching, with a $100 million top-up adding to the existing $70 million budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To provide more support for our charities amidst COVID-19, the Government will partner the Tote Board to enhance the matching for donations through Tote Board's Enhanced Fund-raising Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Charities can apply to receive dollar-for-dollar matching on eligible donations, which are raised from projects in FY2020, up to a cap of $250,000 per charity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To enable this, I will provide a top-up of $100 million, to add to the existing $70 million budget for the Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme.

sections.label: Invictus Fund top-up
sections.summary: A top-up of $18 million will be provided to the Invictus Fund to enhance support for social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To enhance support for our social service agencies, I will provide a top-up of $18 million to the Invictus Fund.

sections.label: FY2020 Overall Budget deficit
sections.summary: The Overall Budget deficit for FY2020 will increase to $74.3 billion, or 15.4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Overall Budget deficit for FY2020 will increase to $74.3 billion, or 15.4% of GDP.

sections.label: Past Reserves draw for Budget
sections.summary: The President gave in-principle support for a further $31 billion draw from Past Reserves, up to $52 billion this financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The President, in consultation with the CPA, has given her in-principle support for a further draw of $31 billion from our Past Reserves to fund the measures in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Lives and livelihoods continue to be at stake… Having deliberated and considered the recommendation of the CPA, I am satisfied that the fourth support package is necessary… I have therefore given my in-principle support for the proposed measures to draw on the Government's past reserves." Altogether, we are looking at drawing up to a total of $52 billion from Past Reserves this financial year to enable Singaporeans to tide through this crisis and emerge stronger.

sections.label: Additional Contingencies Funds set aside
sections.summary: After briefing Cabinet, the President and the CPA, an additional $13 billion will be set aside in the Contingencies Funds.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Having briefed Cabinet, the President and the CPA, I will set aside an additional $13 billion in the Contingencies Funds.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget total
sections.summary: The Fortitude Budget totaling $33 billion is put forth to ameliorate pandemic impacts and help everyone adapt.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To ameliorate the impacts of the pandemic and to help everyone adapt to this new normal, I am putting forth this Fortitude Budget totaling $33 billion.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: The Government will launch the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package to create 100,000 jobs, traineeships and skill training opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will launch the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package to create 100,000 jobs, traineeships and skill training opportunities, in partnership with the business associations and unions.

sections.label: Cash grant and rental relief
sections.summary: The Government will provide a cash grant and legislate to provide rental relief to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will also provide a cash grant and legislate to provide rental relief to SMEs.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme extension
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme will be extended by a month until August.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, we will also extend the Jobs Support Scheme by a month until August.

sections.label: Digital Resilience Bonus and COVID-19 Support Grant
sections.summary: The Government will set aside over $500 million for a Digital Resilience Bonus and other measures, and an additional $800 million for the COVID-19 Support Grant, which has received 48,000 applications.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As such, the Government will set aside more than $500 million to provide a Digital Resilience Bonus and other support measures to accelerate the firms' digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government has received 48,000 applications for the COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will set aside an additional $800 million for this to help Singaporeans who have been displaced from their jobs or have their incomes affected.

sections.label: Four Budgets COVID-19 spending
sections.summary: Through four Budgets this year, the Government has committed almost $100 billion to battle COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Through these four Budgets this year, the Government has committed almost $100 billion to battle COVID-19.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget focus and business support
sections.summary: The Fortitude Budget focuses on saving jobs and supporting workers, with larger businesses able to bring forward procurement and payment schedules, and the Emerging Stronger Task force charting a path in a changed world.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The key focus of this Fortitude Budget, building on the last three Budgets, is to provide resources for us to make decisive moves to save jobs and support our workers – now and for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Larger businesses can bring forward procurement and payment schedules to help their suppliers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, the Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry has formed a COVID-19 task force to raise funds to support their micro-SME members.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, the Emerging Stronger Task force is partnering business leaders, SME owners, industry experts and TACs to chart our path in a changed world.

sections.label: Naming of Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: The Budget is named Fortitude Budget because our generation must persevere, adapt and emerge stronger, like the founding generation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our generation must have the fortitude to persevere, to adapt and emerge stronger, just like our founding generation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is why I have named this our Fortitude Budget – courage in adversity.

sections.label: Deficit, reserves and Contingencies Fund
sections.summary: The Budget projects a $74.3 billion deficit, draws $52 billion from past reserves, sets aside $13 billion in the Contingencies Fund, and dedicates $92.9 billion or almost 20% of GDP to fight the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Never in our wildest dream would we imagine the House to scrutinise a Budget that project an overall deficit of $74.3 billion, drawing on our past reserves for a total of $52 billion and utilising almost all our current term's reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given the uncertainties that are still ahead of us, a further additional $13 billion is set aside in the Contingencies Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In total, $92.9 billion or almost 20% of our GDP is dedicated to support our people to fight the pandemic.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme share
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme alone accounts for about $23.5 billion of the entire $92 billion fiscal package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) itself alone accounts for about $23.5 billion of the entire $92 billion fiscal package.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: The fourth Budget introduced a $2 billion SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package targeting about 100,000 opportunities, 40,000 jobs, 25,000 traineeships and 30,000 skills training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, we need a whole-of-eco-system effort to create new jobs and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And I am glad that this fourth Budget further introduced a massive $2 billion SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package where the Government commits to a further stretched target of creating about 100,000 opportunities, 40,000 jobs, 25,000 traineeships and 30,000 skills training.

sections.label: Companies retaining telecommute arrangements
sections.summary: Some companies are looking to retain telecommute arrangements so many employees can keep working from home after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, some companies are now looking to retain many of the telecommute arrangements so that a significant number of their employees can continue to work from home even after COVID-19.

sections.label: E-payment and digitalisation support
sections.summary: The fourth Budget offers a $300 monthly bonus over five months for stallholders adopting e-payments and a $5,000 Digital Resilience Bonus under the enhanced SMEs Go Digital package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, this what the fourth Budget has also set out to do, such as the $300 per month bonus over five months to encourage stallholders in the neigbourhood to adopt e-payments and to avoid cash handling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There is also the enhancing the SMEs Go Digital package to include a $5,000 Digital Resilience Bonus to help businesses with entry level upgrades, such as payroll, e-invoicing, e-payments and other e-commerce solutions.

sections.label: Digital Ambassadors for seniors and stallholders
sections.summary: MCI is recruiting 1,000 Digital Ambassadors and aims to raise the digital skills of 100,000 seniors by March 2021 through one-on-one efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Here is a case where we must go down right to the last 5% and get everyone onboard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And I am very glad that MCI is doubling down on these efforts, with the announcement to recruit 1,000 Digital Ambassadors to help seniors and local stallholders be digitally enabled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Their quality of life can improve if they are also digitally connected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I salute MCI for setting the ambitious target of reaching out and raising the digital skills of 100,000 seniors by March 2021, in less than one year, through one-on-one efforts.

sections.label: Migrant worker dormitory outbreak response
sections.summary: The Government, MOM, SAF, stakeholders and volunteers responded expeditiously and extensively to stabilise the outbreak among 400,000 migrant workers in dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I want to specifically mention those that have worked very hard in the last few months to manage and contain the outbreak at the migrant workers' dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is a gigantic task to take care of the health and well-being of 400,000 migrant workers – a massive and complex operation that require both scale and speed of response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While we would rather not have so many cases of infections at the dormitories, the expeditious and extensive response by the Government, which includes MOM, SAF, other stakeholders as well as volunteers to stabilise the outbreak demonstrates the strength, the versatility and the tenacity of Team Singapore.

sections.label: Question on contingency fund scope
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Deputy Prime Minister about the scope of usage of the $16 billion contingency fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Before I end, I would like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister a question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: He mentioned about the $16 billion contingency fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is the scope of the usage of the fund?

sections.label: Homes and domestic violence rise
sections.summary: Small or overcrowded homes are unpleasant, and police-recorded domestic violence rose 22% since circuit breaker measures while AWARE's April family violence calls more than doubled from last April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Homes that are small or overcrowded are unpleasant environments to remain in for most of the day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported that domestic violence cases recorded by the Singapore Police rose by 22% since the circuit breaker measures started while the NGO, AWARE, disclosed that calls about family violence in April this year were more than double those of April last year.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Task Force gender imbalance
sections.summary: The Government formed an Emerging Stronger Task Force of 17 eminent persons, but only two of the 17 members are women, 11%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the Government has put together an Emerging Stronger Task Force consisting of 17 eminent persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the membership of the Task Force has a gender imbalance with only two women out of 17 – a dismal 11%.

sections.label: SIRS income support and appeals
sections.summary: SIRS was announced in the Resilience Budget, promising nine months of income support to eligible self-employed persons at $1,000 per month, and more than 60,000 appeals were received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SIRS was announced in the Resilience Budget, promising nine months of income support to eligible self-employed persons at $1,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since then, as SIRS has been rolled out, we were told that more than 60,000 appeals had been received.

sections.label: SIRS auto-inclusion and reduced payments
sections.summary: SIRS is an auto-inclusion scheme not requiring proof of income loss, so full payments went to self-employed persons whose incomes were unaffected by COVID-19, and some appeals led to reduced payments of $800 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the other hand, SIRS is an auto-inclusion scheme that does not require the self-employed person to show income loss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The design of SIRS has thus also resulted in full SIRS payments being made to self-employed persons whose incomes are unaffected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In some cases, appeals resulted in payment of a reduced amount, at $800 per month instead of $1,000 per month.

sections.label: MOM and NTUC scheme roles
sections.summary: The Government stated that MOM oversees the scheme while NTUC helps administer appeals for those who do not automatically qualify.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has stated that MOM oversees the scheme but NTUC helps administer appeals for those who do not automatically qualify.

sections.label: SingPass tied to one phone number
sections.summary: Even if family members were willing to assist, each SingPass could only be tied to one phone number.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Furthermore, even if family members were willing to assist, each SingPass could only be tied to one phone number.

sections.label: Unemployment, GDP and Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: Unemployment rose to 3.3% and revised GDP is forecasted between -7% and -4%, while the $33 billion Fortitude Budget emphasises preparing people and businesses and saving and creating jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While still low, unemployment has risen to 3.3% and the economic impact is not trivial with the latest revised GDP for Singapore forecasted to be between -7% and -4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the $33 billion Fortitude Budget extends more help to support individuals and households in the fight against COVID-19, the emphasis of the Fortitude Budget is on measures to enable our people and businesses to get ready for what lies ahead and to save and create jobs.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: The $2 billion SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package provides 40,000 jobs, 25,000 traineeships, 30,000 training places and hiring incentives, with traineeships helping new graduates gain industry experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The $2 billion SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package with 40,000 jobs, 25,000 traineeships and 30,000 training places and hiring incentives is much needed and will provide quality jobs and programmes for those seeking employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the current economic conditions, the traineeship schemes will help new graduates entering the workforce find opportunities in emerging and growing sectors and this will allow them to gain valuable industry experience.

sections.label: Circuit breaker and telecommuting
sections.summary: Circuit breaker measures required more companies to adopt telecommuting, and more jobs can be expected to adopt flexible work arrangements as a norm even after circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For example, the circuit breaker measures have required more companies to adopt telecommuting and although the jury is out, we can expect more jobs to adopt flexible work arrangements as a norm rather than an option even after circuit breaker.

sections.label: Engagerocket work-from-home survey
sections.summary: In a Straits Times report on an Engagerocket survey, 90% of respondents wished to continue working from home in some capacity, but more than half said their productivity had dropped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In the recent Straits Times report on a survey conducted by Engagerocket, 90% of the respondents indicated that they wished to continue working from home in some capacity even after the circuit breaker ends.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But despite this willingness, more than half indicated their productivity had dropped and was lower.

sections.label: Digital inclusion in Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: An important priority of the Fortitude Budget is digital inclusion, with attention on students from lower income families, seniors, smaller businesses and hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: An important priority of the Fortitude Budget is digital inclusion with attention on students from lower income families, seniors and the smaller businesses and hawkers.

sections.label: Senior Go Digital Movement
sections.summary: Digitalisation entails new behaviours for individuals, families and businesses, and the passage calls the investment in the Senior Go Digital Movement a brilliant move supporting digital adoption for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Digitalisation, as I have mentioned, entails new behaviours whether for individuals, families, businesses large or small, as we have witnessed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, it is indeed a brilliant move and I really must say that it is indeed a brilliant move and a commitment to invest in the Senior Go Digital Movement to support digital adoption for seniors.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget funding and reserves
sections.summary: The passage states the Fortitude Budget funding is needed and welcomed but cannot go on indefinitely, and that reserves, not borrowing, funded the support package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the funding from the Fortitude Budget is needed and welcomed, we have to also recognise that it cannot go on indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We are fortunate with prudent management that our Government has built up on our reserves and we did not have to borrow to fund such a significant support package.

sections.label: Support for Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: The passage states many companies and workers are struggling, and the speaker supports the Fortitude Budget to keep companies afloat and Singaporeans in jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Many companies are at breaking point and many workers are struggling to cope.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I support the Fortitude Budget, as I have the previous three, because it will keep companies afloat and it will keep Singaporeans in their jobs.

sections.label: Realism about $100 billion Budget
sections.summary: The passage states that even with the $100 billion total Budget, there is a need to be realistic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Even with the $100 billion total Budget, we need to be realistic.

sections.label: Anxieties and protecting jobs
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker senses anxieties through online chats and that three things can and must be done to protect jobs and keep workers safe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I can sense their anxieties even across the cyber domain when I chat with them on the different media.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: There are three things we can and must do to protect our jobs and keep our workers safe.

sections.label: Restarting economy with financial muscle
sections.summary: The passage states community infection has been stabilised and lives safeguarded, and the economy is restarting with $100 billion worth of financial muscle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We have stabilised the community infection and safeguarded lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We are now restarting the economy with $100 billion worth of financial muscle on the table.

sections.label: Helping taxi drivers at Newton Circle
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker and Minister Khaw met taxi drivers at Newton Circle hawker centre whose incomes were impacted by 50% or more, and $77 million was put up to help drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I remember going to Newton Circle hawker centre with Minister Khaw to talk to taxi drivers, because their incomes were impacted, at that time, by already 50% or more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We set up a quick reaction small group and put up $77 million to help our drivers cope with the initial hit of COVID-19.

sections.label: Training on Safe Management Measures
sections.summary: Over 1,800 union leaders, management partners and staff were trained on Safe Management Measures to help employers keep workers safe and businesses open.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To date, we had played another part to lead in terms of training over 1,800 union leaders, our management partners and staff on Safe Management Measures so that we can partner employers in companies to implement Safe Management Measures to keep workers safe and importantly, to keep businesses open.

sections.label: Job Support Scheme expansion
sections.summary: The Government's Job Support Scheme helped businesses with wage costs, and NTUC's Secretary-General thanked the Government for expanding it in severely impacted industries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Government's Job Support Scheme (JSS) has helped many businesses manage part of the wage cost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As the Secretary-General, I thank the Government for responding to NTUC's feedback to expand JSS in more severely impacted industries.

sections.label: NTUC LearningHub May training
sections.summary: In May, NTUC LearningHub helped over 500 companies send workers for over 20,000 days of training, with up to $80 a day in absentee payroll per worker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In May alone, NTUC LearningHub helped more than 500 companies who sent their workers for over 20,000 days' worth of training, these companies received up to $80 a day in absentee payroll for each worker they sent.

sections.label: Matching aviation workers to jobs
sections.summary: NTUC partnered aviation companies to match workers into new jobs, and its Job Security Council has matched more than 10,000 workers into new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: At the earlier stages, we moved quickly to partner badly hit aviation companies to match workers to new jobs – some into community work, some into healthcare and some even into our own NTUC FairPrice Group – without the workers having to go through retrenchment anxieties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: So far, NTUC's Job Security Council has been able to match more than 10,000 workers, both rank-and-file and PMEs, into new jobs – easing workers' anxiety and most importantly, helping them earn a wage to sustain livelihood.

sections.label: Jobs, traineeships and skills programmes
sections.summary: The Government and employers aim to create 40,000 jobs, with 25,000 SGUnited Traineeships and 30,000 SGUnited Skills training spaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Foremost, the Government and employers' role to create 40,000 jobs is critical, not easy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: And where companies are not able to do so, the 25,000 SGUnited Traineeships programme will be helpful to expose both new graduates and mid-career PMEs to the new workplace, gain useful experience and be ready when the economy recovers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The 30,000 training spaces under the SGUnited Skills Programme will be helpful to top up skills for workers looking for jobs.

sections.label: Job Security Council growth and matches
sections.summary: Over four months, companies in the Job Security Council grew to over 7,000, and 10,000 workers were matched to new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Over the past four months, the number of companies in the Job Security Council has increased to over 7,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: More importantly, we have successfully matched 10,000 workers to new jobs.

sections.label: Unity, jobs and economy post-COVID
sections.summary: A strategy backed by robust Budgets aims to preserve and create jobs, match workers to jobs, and push industry transformation post-COVID.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I believe that if we stay united, we will be able to sustain our businesses, protect our workers and secure our future!

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We have a strategy in place, backed up by a series of robust Budgets, making the necessary resources available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the immediate term – preserve jobs, create jobs and match workers to these jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: But we must keep an eye out too on strengthening our economy post-COVID.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We must make use of this crisis to push for industry transformation and continue developing quality jobs for quality workers and quality busineses that can out-compete in the new economy forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: NTUC will continue to work with our tripartite partners to support our workers, our freelancers, our self-employed people – because every worker matters, every job matters.

sections.label: NTUC role in SIRS appeals
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether NTUC decided the appeal criteria for SIRS, noting guidelines were worked within for policy questions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Earlier in his response to my query, he basically said that it made sense for NTUC to be involved in SIRS because it has some understanding of the issues faced by self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Could he clarify in this SIRS appeal process, were the appeal criteria – what factors are relevant to grant or partially grant appeals – decided by NTUC?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: That means NTUC came up with appeals criteria?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: So, for the policy questions, the criteria, we have certain guidelines that we worked within.

sections.label: Plight of mid-career workers
sections.summary: The speaker says the speech highlights three areas, the third being the plight of mid-career workers, especially Professionals, Managers and Executives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: But I thought to use my speech to highlight three important areas, which we should look at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: And thirdly, to highlight the plight of mid-career workers, in particular, the Professionals, Managers and Executives.

sections.label: Unilateral salary and work hour changes
sections.summary: The speaker shares horror stories of unilateral withdrawal or reduction of salaries and work hours without consultation or agreement with the worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Just to share some of these horror stories that I have heard from many of these workers during this past eight weeks and moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is a stark wake-up call, particularly because in situations where this has happened, it is a situation where there was no consultation with the worker and no agreement with the worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: That is one example – a unilateral withdrawal or reduction of salaries and work hours.

sections.label: Disguised retrenchment without compensation
sections.summary: A disguised retrenchment scenario is described where a worker is contractually terminated without reason and not adequately compensated with retrenchment benefit or severance pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Sometimes, the reason happens because of a disguised retrenchment scenario, that is, the worker may be contractually terminated without reason, and subsequently, after he or she has left the company, realised that that particular slot was left vacant, totally vacant, and not filled up, which means there was a redundancy situation and they were not adequately compensated with retrenchment benefit or severance pay.

sections.label: Reviewing advisories and employment laws
sections.summary: The speaker stresses working together to review advisories, National Wages Council recommendations, and employment laws for the new normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I cannot emphasise more the importance for us to work together, in particular, in reviewing some of these advisories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It could be the National Wages Council's recommendations or some advisories and guidelines to ensure and, even perhaps moving ahead, to review some of the employment laws because of the "new normal" that we are having to operate in and some of the new rules and more people working from home.

sections.label: Support for mid-career workers
sections.summary: The speaker worries for workers and notes Budgets focused on mid-career workers and PMETs through schemes like Career Support Programme and Adapt-and-Grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With this whole game-change and "next normal", I really fear and worry for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that in the Fortitude Budget – and not just in this Fortitude Budget, even at the first Budget that we had – we focused a lot on mid-career workers, in particular the PMETs – through the Career Support Programme, Adapt-and-Grow and a whole slew of measures.

sections.label: Wage support percentages
sections.summary: Help for mid-career workers includes 20% for six months and 40% for six months for those above 40.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In terms of helping mid-career workers – 20% for six months, the 40% for six months for those above 40.

sections.label: Employers embracing job schemes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes more employers embrace schemes and urges Government to support companies with strong Singaporean Core and progressive practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Though they are a small group but there are still opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: And I hope that through this Budget and all these measures and, of course, with a close partnership amongst the tripartite partners and the newly formed National Jobs Council, we hope more employers will step forward to embrace some of these schemes – not just the traineeship programmes but, at the same time, if they have openings, if they have opportunities, to latch on some of these useful schemes and support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Government as well, for those companies that have this strong hiring or strengthening of Singaporean Core, at the same time, a strong support of some of these schemes and good practices, not just good, not just fair, not just responsible, but progressive practices, I hope the Government can give these companies a pat on the back and also more and greater support so that they will be encouraged to do even more.

sections.label: Tripartite partners pivoting together
sections.summary: The speaker says tripartite partners must work together to pivot and grab opportunities, stressing every worker matters and jobs and workplaces must stay safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the bigger picture, on the national front, how we, as tripartite partners, can work together – Government, NTUC and all the employers – so that we are able to pivot, rise to the challenge and at same time, also grab the new opportunities that come before us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: And on this note, I cannot emphasise more – every worker matters, every job counts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My speech will focus on keeping our jobs and our workplaces safe because failing to do so may result in another unwelcome spike in COVID-19 cases and undo all our efforts and the billions of dollars that we have committed and are committing to tide our nation through this crisis.

sections.label: Businesses facing differing requirements
sections.summary: Many businesses and workers have faced different requirements and instructions from different Government agencies over past months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many businesses and their workers have been facing different requirements and different sets of instructions from different Government agencies over the past months.

sections.label: Testing for construction and care staff
sections.summary: Construction workers must be tested every two weeks, while pre-school and nursing home staff took a precautionary test before returning to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Today, construction workers are required to be tested every two weeks, while pre-school and nursing home staff have taken a precautionary test before returning to work.

sections.label: Robots and unsafe business products
sections.summary: Robots have been deployed in community isolation facilities, but some businesses market products that may do more harm than good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We too have deployed similar robots in our community isolation facilities and elsewhere in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I am deeply concerned that some businesses are marketing products that may end up doing more harm than good.

sections.label: Harmful UV light products
sections.summary: Products causing prolonged UV light exposure are harmful, and the Government is urged to review and stop unsafe interventions at workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Other products, which could cause prolonged UV light exposure, are also harmful to the human body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I therefore urge the Government to review and where necessary, stop the use of such unsafe interventions at our workplaces.

sections.label: Mental health spending and psychiatrists
sections.summary: Mental health is under 5% of MOH operating expenditure, with 4.4 psychiatrists per 100,000 people versus 15 in most OECD countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The total expenditure on mental health makes up less than 5% of MOH's annual operating expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Within the population, Singapore has an estimated average of 4.4 psychiatrists for every 100,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This figure is much lower than the 15 psychiatrists per 100,000 recorded by most OECD countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Companies are now required to appoint Safe Management Officers (SMOs) before they can resume work and NTUC has already trained over 1,700 to be SMOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We aim to double that number in the coming months.

sections.label: COVID-19 relief measures funding
sections.summary: With an additional $33 billion in relief measures, the Government has set aside close to $100 billion to support Singaporeans against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the additional $33 billion in relief measures, the Government has now set aside close to $100 billion to support Singaporeans in our fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: SMF survey on safety and health
sections.summary: In a recent SMF survey, 62% of members ranked safety and health as their top concern, with some reporting a near four-fold rise in monthly cleaning expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, in a recent survey of members of the SMF, 62% of the members surveyed ranked safety and health as their top concern as they prepare for the reopening of more businesses after the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some members have even indicated an almost four-fold increase in monthly cleaning expenses to ensure a clean environment for their workers and products.

sections.label: Quarantine and overseas contractual obligations
sections.summary: Workers face 14-day quarantine on each side, totalling 28 days unable to work, and businesses cannot fully fulfil overseas contractual obligations due to circuit breaker measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One area is the 14-day quarantine or Stay-Home Notice that workers going to and returning from either country face on each side, making it a total of 28 days that the worker is not able to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On overseas contractual obligations – another key concern for businesses is their inability to fully fulfill their contractual obligations to overseas clients due to circuit breaker measures.

sections.label: SMF seeks global legal framework
sections.summary: The SMF advocates for the Government to lead efforts to get other countries to agree on a legal framework that transcends jurisdictional boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, the SMF would like to advocate for the Government to take the lead and work towards getting agreement from other countries on a legal framework that transcends jurisdictional boundaries, much along the lines of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act.

sections.label: Digital adoption barriers for SMF members
sections.summary: Since the circuit breaker, expressions of interest nearly matched those from August 2018 to April 2020, while a 2020 SMF survey cited uncertain returns, lack of technical capabilities and cybersecurity concerns as barriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since the circuit breaker, we have seen almost the same number of expressions of interest as in the months from August 2018 to April 2020, when the programme was launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a survey of the members of SMF conducted in early 2020, members cited uncertain return of investment, lack of technical capabilities as well as concerns on cybersecurity as key reasons holding them back from adopting digital technologies.

sections.label: Upskilling older workers language courses
sections.summary: Members highlighted challenges upskilling this age group as most courses are in English and few are in Chinese, Malay or Tamil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Members have since highlighted that there is a challenge in upskilling their workforce in this age group as most courses are conducted in English and there is a relative scarcity of courses conducted in Chinese, Malay or Tamil that this age group of workers may be more comfortable with.

sections.label: SMF commitment to solidarity and resilience
sections.summary: The SMF commits to stand in solidarity and unity with members and the Government, increase business resilience and surmount difficulties with fortitude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a partner in nation building, the SMF is committed to stand in Solidarity and Unity with our members and the Government, increase business Resilience and surmount this difficulty with Fortitude.

sections.label: FairPrice response at COVID-19 onset
sections.summary: In the Solidarity Budget debate speech, the speaker shared how NTUC FairPrice Group responded at the onset of COVID-19 to assure consumers on essentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In my speech at the debate on the Solidarity Budget, I shared how NTUC FairPrice Group proactively responded at the onset of COVID-19 to assure consumers and public on the availability and affordability of essentials.

sections.label: FairPrice added 4,000 staff
sections.summary: Over two months, FairPrice Group provided employment for an additional 4,000 full-time, part-time and temporary staff, including Ms Gina Ng, arranged through the Job Security Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Over the last two months, FairPrice group has provided employment opportunities for an additional 4,000 staff – full time, part-time and temporary workers – to support operations and the high transaction volume that we experience and this includes people like Ms Gina Ng, a lady that Mr Ng Chee Meng referred to just now and, indeed, this was arranged though the Job Security Council.

sections.label: Filling 300 more positions
sections.summary: Stints end in July and August; 300 more positions are being filled, and NTUC Enterprise will offer 300 training places under the SGUnited Traineeships Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Their stints will end some in July and some in August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We are currently looking to fill another 300 more positions and working with other agencies to provide employment for workers, especially those who have been displaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC Enterprise group will certainly be supporting the SGUnited Traineeships Scheme and offer 300 training places to help trainees in exposure and experience in the various areas of business.

sections.label: Online courses and digital initiatives
sections.summary: NTUC LearningHub provided online courses covering Adaptive and Technological Skills, and during the circuit breaker LearningHub's free online courses got close to 70,000 sign-ups while Kidzmatters got 90,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: To encourage all our workers to make good use of time to upgrade their skillsets, NTUC LearningHub has provided access to online courses that covers both Adaptive Skills and Technological Skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: During this circuit breaker period, two of our NTUC Social Enterprises quickly pivoted and launched new digital initiatives: LearningHub introduced free online courses, which received close to 70,000 sign-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: On the other hand, our NTUC First Campus also launched “Kidzmatters” for parents, and this received 90,000 sign-ups.

sections.label: FairPrice circuit breaker initiatives
sections.summary: During the circuit breaker, FairPrice set up pop-up and atrium stores, increased online capacity, and instituted a priority shopping hour for the Pioneer Generation and vulnerables.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: During the circuit breaker period, to cope with the continued surge in demand and provide greater convenience to customers, FairPrice had to develop various solutions and initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: They include the setting up of pop-up and atrium stores, increasing online capacity, and instituting a "priority shopping hour" for the Pioneer Generation and vulnerables.

sections.label: FairPrice on Wheels locations
sections.summary: FairPrice on Wheels is now in eight locations and growing to grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: FairPrice on Wheels is now in eight locations and growing to grow.

sections.label: NTUC Enterprise support package
sections.summary: The NTUC Enterprise group of social enterprises led by FairPrice will put together a package to help Singaporeans and families for the services they are involved in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The NTUC Enterprise group of social enterprises led by FairPrice will be putting together a package to help Singaporeans and families address this for the services that we are involved.

sections.label: Singapore GDP and affected sectors
sections.summary: Singapore's GDP growth is expected at -7% to -4%, with manufacturing, wholesale trade and transportation and storage adversely affected by slowdowns in key markets and global supply chain disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As a small and open economy, Singapore’s GDP growth is expected to come in at -7% to -4%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Sectors such as manufacturing, wholesale trade and transportation and storage will be adversely affected by the sharper-than-expected slowdown in many of Singapore’s key markets and there will be prolonged uncertainties as well disruptions in the global supply chains.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: The new SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package will create close to 100,000 placement opportunities in jobs, traineeships and training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To help workers stay employed and employable, the new SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package will create close to 100,000 placement opportunities in the three areas of jobs, traineeships and training.

sections.label: NTUC JSC network and placements
sections.summary: NTUC JSC has more than 7,000 companies in its network and has emplaced more than 10,000 workers into job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: NTUC JSC, as Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng has shared earlier, has more than 7,000 companies in our network and has emplaced more than 10,000 workers into job opportunities.

sections.label: DKA cross-skilling aviation workers
sections.summary: DKA will use COVID-19 downtime to cross-skill workers through structured on-the-job training so workers can be re-deployed and the company emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: While DKA's business in the aviation sector has been affected by COVID-19, they will be using this downtime to cross-skill workers through structured on-the-job training so that they have flexibility to re-deploy workers to areas of need and emerge stronger from the crisis.

sections.label: Virtual OTR with A*STAR
sections.summary: Because COVID-19 prevents physical OTR sessions, NTUC worked with A*STAR to develop a virtual-OTR methodology and began it with Certact Engineering.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, due to COVID-19, physical OTR sessions cannot be conducted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Hence, NTUC worked with A*STAR to develop a virtual-OTR methodology and we embarked on this virtual OTR process with Certact Engineering recently.

sections.label: NTUC training fund support increases
sections.summary: NTUC increased the NCF training support cap from S$30,000 to S$50,000 per unionised company and introduced NCF-Lite for non-unionised companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: NTUC introduced the NTUC-Education and Training Fund (NETF) Collaborative Fund (NCF) in March 2019 to provide training-related funding support to our unionised companies who send their unionised employees for training programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To help the increasing number of affected workers and to ensure that training costs to companies are further reduced during this COVID-19 period, I am glad to share that NTUC has increased the training support funding cap of this NCF from S$30,000 to S$50,000 per unionised company.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To speed up business recovery, we will also introduce NETF Collaborative Fund Lite or NCF-Lite, for non-unionised companies with 50 or more NTUC union members in their workforce, with training support of up to $8,000 per company.

sections.label: Government Budget support for businesses
sections.summary: The Government has set aside nearly $100 billion through the four Budgets to support both businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government has set aside nearly $100 billion through the four Budgets to support both businesses and workers.

sections.label: Driver Care Fund for part-time drivers
sections.summary: Part-time private hire drivers not qualifying for daily rental rebates received a $300 Driver Care Fund, administered by NTUC, benefiting over 3,500 drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Part-time private hire drivers who do not qualify for the daily rental rebates under the Special Relief Fund was given a $300 Driver Care Fund which the Ministry provides for part-time driver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: NTUC helped administered the Fund and over 3,500 drivers have benefited from that scheme.

sections.label: Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme
sections.summary: The $9,000 Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme helped 130,000 SEPs who auto-qualify under eligibility criteria deal with sudden income drop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To help them deal with a sudden drop in income, we heard earlier about the $9,000 Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: SIRS, based on eligibility criteria, benefited 130,000 SEPs who are auto-qualify to benefit.

sections.label: Contribute-As-You-Earn MediSave initiative
sections.summary: MOM's Contribute-As-You-Earn initiative helps SEPs contribute to MediSave, but is early-stage and has not reached many of Singapore's 200,000 SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOM had earlier launched the Contribute-As-You-Earn initiative to help SEPs contribute regularly into their MediSave account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, it is only in its early stage and has not reached many of the 200,000 SEPs in Singapore.

sections.label: Job-matching for self-employed persons
sections.summary: NTUC's Employment & Employability Institute conducts job-matching for self-employed persons seeking temporary jobs or career switches after losing income from COVID-19 restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many lost their income when their clients stopped buying services from them because of restrictions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The NTUC's Employment & Employability Institute has been conducting job-matching for self-employed persons who would like to consider temporary jobs or make a career switch.

sections.label: Drivers moving to new roles
sections.summary: Drivers have become bus captains, emcees, tour guides, screeners or swabbers, and over 10,000 taxi and private hire drivers now deliver food, groceries and parcels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have spoken to many drivers, taxi drivers and private hire drivers, who have changed career tracks and become bus captains as well as event emcees and tour guides, who have taken on temporary roles as temperature screeners or swabbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Also, we read recently that over 10,000 taxi and private hire drivers have moved from serving commuters to delivering food, groceries and parcels – this is thanks to the MOT's help to liberalise the current point-to-point regulations.

sections.label: Supporting self-employed persons workforce
sections.summary: Businesses, service buyers and Government can support self-employed persons by looking beyond contractual relationships to keep the workforce viable after the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Due to the pandemic, more of us have begun to better understand the needs of the over 200,000 self-employed persons in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: All businesses and service buyers, and yes, including Government as buyers, can help by looking beyond the boundaries of contractual relationships and support our self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is imperative that we work towards ensuring that the self-employed persons workforce that contributes significantly to the development of many sectors remain viable and intact even after the pandemic has ended.

sections.label: Outsourced industries workforce characteristics
sections.summary: Outsourced industries under the Progressive Wage Model have older workers, low technology use, low productivity, foreign manpower reliance, and bottom-fifth-percentile salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, most of the companies in the outsourced industries where the Progressive Wage Model is made mandatory, are characterised by an older workforce, limited use of technology, relatively low productivity, heavy reliance on foreign manpower, and their salaries hover at the bottom fifth percentile of the resident workforce in terms of gross monthly salary.

sections.label: PWM bonus for workers
sections.summary: Cleaners and landscape workers get two weeks of PWM bonus, security officers get none, and a one-month annual bonus would raise wage increment by about 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, under the mandatory Progessive Wage Model (PWM), our cleaners and landscape workers are given only two weeks of PWM bonus but, there is none for the security officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Simply giving them an annual bonus of one month would increase the percentage of wage increment by about 8%.

sections.label: Recognising environmental services workers as specialists
sections.summary: With higher skills and productivity, environmental services workers, security officers and landscape specialists should be regarded as specialists, not low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With higher skills and greater productivity, these environmental services workers, security officers and landscape specialists should be regarded as specialists in their own respective areas and would not be seen or regarded as low-wage workers.

sections.label: Outcome-based contracting for service procurement
sections.summary: Outcome-based contracting must be the norm, and service buyers should award contracts only to companies with progressive employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Outcome-based Contracting must be the norm for procuring services and service buyers should only award contracts to companies with progressive employment practices that reward and recognise their workers right.

sections.label: ComCare assistance and WIS payments
sections.summary: An OCBC survey found 70% of working adults lack funds beyond six months; the speaker seeks ComCare criteria review and notes WIS recipients welcome $3,000 paid in July and October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
