sentences.text: In a recent survey conducted by OCBC, it was shared that 70% of working adults do not have enough funds to last them beyond six months if they were to lose their jobs now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I would not be surprised if many low-wage workers would fall into this group as they have very little savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like the Government to consider reviewing the criteria for Short to Mid-Term ComCare Assistance to enable more households to be eligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Many WIS recipients welcome the $3000 one-off special cash payment which will be paid over two equal payments of $1,500 each, in July and October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I hope that should the crisis be prolonged, the Government could consider another one-off special payment but perhaps in smaller amount spread over a longer period.

sections.label: Progressive society after crisis spending
sections.summary: If the $100 billion spent in the crisis does not lead to a more progressive, equitable and enlightened future, it would be a tragedy to only survive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If the $100 billion we have spent in this crisis does not lead us to a future where we can be more progressive, more equitable and more enlightened, then indeed it would be a tragedy if the only thing we did was just trying to survive, rather than coming out stronger as a society.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant extension request
sections.summary: An MP asks whether the COVID-19 Support Grant can be extended beyond three months and raised to $1,000 monthly, matching SIRS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the most recent estimate by MTI, Singapore’s GDP is projected to be -7% to -4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a typical business environment, it takes a retrenched worker about three to six months to secure a new job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of this possible impact on workers, can the Government explore making COVID-19 Support Grant a long-term help to provide workers facing short-term unemployment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, can the Government consider extending the length of support beyond three months, with each applicant reassessed every three months based on their past training and job search efforts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we also increase the quantum of assistance to $1,000 per month, aligning with Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) because both employees and the self-employed face the same pressure during the period of unemployment?

sections.label: Economic transformation and regional manufacturing
sections.summary: The passage says the downtime should be used to transform the economy and refocus on regional manufacturing zones as supply chains shift from China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While there might be some short-term pains, it is not all doom and gloom as the recovery will eventually come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must use this downtime strategically to transform our economy and accelerate the push for Industry 4.0 in the various sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As supply chain and global manufacturing start to shift away from China, we need to refocus on regional manufacturing zones, such as Central and Eastern Europe (or CEE) for Europe, Mexico for the Americas, as well as India and South-East Asia countries for Asia.

sections.label: Industry 4.0 and digital transformation
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore's Industry 4.0 transformation progress was slower than expected, but COVID-19 accelerated digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While Singapore has embarked on transforming our economy and our businesses to adopt Industry 4.0 technological advances, the progress is not as fast as we had expected it to be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, with COVID-19, it has accelerated some of these transformations, particularly in the area of digital transformation.

sections.label: Preparing for recession and reform
sections.summary: The passage calls for preparation for recession, resilience, going regional and reform, saying assistance cannot continue indefinitely or keep drawing on Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us be prepared for recession, be resilient, be prepared to go regional and be prepared to reform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This assistance cannot go on indefinitely and we cannot keep drawing down on our Reserves.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements conditions
sections.summary: The passage states that many people are on FWA, which works only with strong care-giving infrastructure and if FWA is pervasive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For the first time since the advent of work have we seen so many people on FWA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But it is also evident that FWA can only work if (a) there is a strong care-giving infrastructure, and (b) FWA must be pervasive.

sections.label: Institutionalising right to FWA
sections.summary: The passage says companies are preparing for permanent telecommuting and that the right to FWA for families should be considered for institutionalising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Many companies, such as Facebook, Twitter and larger banks, are preparing for some of their workforce to be telecommuting permanently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Thus, the pandemic has shown employers that employees cannot be productive without accommodating their family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We must now consider institutionalising the right to FWA for families.

sections.label: Workers in SMEs
sections.summary: The passage states that many workers are in SMEs, that this is an important obstacle to overcome, and that more must be done to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With so many of our workers in SMEs, it is an important obstacle to overcome and we must do more to help them.

sections.label: Changing mindset on childcare subsidies
sections.summary: The passage states that mindsets need to change on a couple of things, and that childcare subsidies have usually been higher for working women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Thus, we will need to change our mindset on a couple of things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have usually given higher childcare subsidies to working women.

sections.label: Student loan repayment relief
sections.summary: The passage states the Resilience Budget's student loan repayment relief is a huge relief for graduating students and hopes for similar relief for PEI students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Resilience Budget's student loan repayment relief is a huge relief for graduating students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We also hope that in this Budget, that the Government can work with private education institutions and banks to provide similar relief for our private education institute (PEI) students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Their tuition fees are unsubsidised and the amount owed can be substantial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Some studies have suggested that students graduating in a recession year earn less than their peers graduating in non-recession years, and that effect continues for a few years.

sections.label: Extending NS for NSFs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether uniformed services could let NSFs with ORD this year extend NS to deepen skills, as training was compromised by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For National Servicemen (NSFs) who are going to have their Operationally Ready Date (ORD) this year, could the uniformed services consider giving them the option to extend their National Service (NS) and deepen their skills since training has been compromised due to COVID-19 and that paramedic and security functions, for example, have continued to be in acute supply?

sections.label: Vacancies and GDP shrinkage
sections.summary: The passage states MOM estimated 60,000 vacancies in late July 2019, and less than a year later annual GDP shrinkage of -4% to -7% is expected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In late July 2019, MOM estimated that there were 60,000 vacancies in our economy waiting to be filled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Now, less than a year later, we are staring at an annual GDP shrinkage of between -4% and -7%.

sections.label: Four Budgets and national reserves
sections.summary: The passage states the anxiety on the ground and that the Government rolled out four Budgets totalling $93 billion, drawing $52 billion from national reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It reflects the serious anxiety we see on the ground – businesses worrying about survival, workers worrying about their jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is why the Government has had to roll out four Budgets totalling $93 billion in as many months, and which entails drawing $52 billion from our national reserves – all unprecedented moves.

sections.label: CPF delay and wage offset
sections.summary: A tripartite agreement delayed CPF contribution rate changes to 2022, and the Government removed the corresponding wage offset.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The tripartite agreement to delay the CPF contribution rate changes from January 2020 to January 2022, the original proposed increases, that agreement to delay is a step in this direction, a step taken in order not to inadvertently raise the risk of retrenchment for older workers aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In delaying the change of the increase, Government also decided to remove the corresponding wage offset which was meant to help employers shoulder half the cost of that CPF increase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I hope that Government can consider re-channelling the $80 million originally earmarked for that transitional offset into strengthening the Senior Employment Credit for the next one year.

sections.label: Hiring incentive for older workers
sections.summary: A six-month hiring incentive for employers hiring local workers aged 40 and above should be extended to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This Incentive targets employers who hire local workers aged 40 and above through eligible re-skilling programmes, and it was meant to last six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I call for the duration of this hiring incentive to be extended from six months to 12 months, in order to make the incentive more attractive to employers to offer job contracts of at least a year to such mature, mid-career job seekers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I also ask Government to consider help – both monetary and non-monetary – to enable organisations, workplaces, to be reshaped to be COVID-safe for workers of all ages, to be age barrier free, with respect to COVID-19.

sections.label: Testing for frontline older workers
sections.summary: The Government is urged to prioritise testing for older workers in frontline occupations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For occupations that employ a large number of older workers at the frontline, I urge the Government to prioritise testing for these workers.

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign Grant
sections.summary: The WorkPro Job Redesign Grant of up to $300,000 per company can be reviewed and re-energised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: What is different though is that current times provide the opportunity to take this up, because companies now can see for themselves the obvious need, advantage and imperative of doing so; it increases competitiveness, enhances resilience, attractiveness, increase your flexibility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And here, the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant of up to $300,000 per company can be reviewed and re-energised to spur action in this harsh but opportune moment.

sections.label: Training older workers digitally
sections.summary: Employers should give older workers fair training access, especially digital training, and older workers should learn new skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Give these older workers, your older workers, a fair go at training, especially training that makes them digitally employable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: When the dust settles, countries that best invest in their workforce and infrastructure to be fighting fit in a very digital future are likely to out-compete the rest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The enlightened employer will continue investing in sharpening the skills of his older workers just as he does his younger ones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The ageist employer will deny his older workers the opportunities to keep current and they will rust away, just as he predicted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I therefore call on employers to adopt a progressive mindset.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, likewise, I urge my fellow older workers to be enthusiastic about learning new skills to stay employable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew, speaking at the 1966 National Day Rally, said "Never be depressed, never be deflated by setbacks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is one of the greatest strengths about Singapore: its willingness to face reality… not because we wished it to be but because it was.

sections.label: Foreign workers in Singapore
sections.summary: Foreign workers rose from about 21,000 in 1970 to about 1.42 million in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1970, there were about 21,000 foreign workers in Singapore making up just above 3% of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2019, the number was closer to 1.42 million, which is about 38% of our labour force.

sections.label: Foreign labour in construction
sections.summary: Construction has nearly 300,000 work permit holders, and foreign labour makes up nearly four in five construction workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Consider the sector at the heart of our COVID-19 outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are nearly 300,000 work permit holders in construction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Including other work passes, foreign labour accounts for nearly four out of every five workers in construction.

sections.label: Low wages for some workers
sections.summary: Median wages for cleaners, F&B assistants and maintenance workers are below $1,500 a month, with benefits and conditions sometimes poor.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Median wages for cleaners, F&B assistants and maintenance workers are below $1,500 a month and employment benefits and conditions of work can be poor.

sections.label: World Bank Malaysia immigration report
sections.summary: A 2013 World Bank report found migrant labour improved employment and wages for medium to high-skilled Malaysians but had negative effects for the lowest skilled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2013, the World Bank released a report on immigration in Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The World Bank found that migrant labour improved employment and wages for medium to high-skilled Malaysians.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, there were also negative effects for the lowest skilled Malaysians.

sections.label: COVID-19 efforts and reserves
sections.summary: Government, healthcare and volunteer efforts forestalled a humanitarian disaster in migrant worker dormitories, and reserves were committed to preserve Singaporean jobs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The unceasing efforts of the Government, healthcare system and volunteers have forestalled what could have been a humanitarian disaster in our migrant worker dormitories due to the COVID-19 outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have also committed vast sums from the reserves to preserve as many Singaporean jobs as possible and to help provide for those whose jobs cannot be saved.

sections.label: Malaysian border closure impact
sections.summary: The ongoing Malaysian border closure forced Malaysian day workers to choose between families and jobs, a blow mitigated by the circuit breaker's temporary hibernation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The on-going closure of the Malaysian border, which has forced our Malaysian day workers to choose between their families and their jobs, has dealt a blow mitigated only by the temporary hibernation of our economy during the circuit breaker.

sections.label: Broadening economic restructuring representation
sections.summary: The speaker suggests broadening representation on the Emerging Stronger Task Force and National Jobs Council and engaging the public as equal partners in economic restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unlike many countries worldwide, economic restructuring and transformation is an integral part of our public spending to deal with COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But we would be shortsighted to assume that our own entrenched interests, our implicit assumptions, our comfort with the existing economic structure play no role in affecting the quality of our judgments about the path ahead.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I therefore suggest that we broaden representation on the councils that we have set up – the Emerging Stronger Task Force and the National Jobs Council – beyond just the captains of industry and state.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should consider having members from the rank and file, the essential services, social services, civil society and academia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And we must engage the public in this great exercise of economic restructuring – not as a public consultation exercise, but as equal partners in the creation of a new Singapore.

sections.label: Bigger home-grown companies
sections.summary: Asks about larger home-grown companies with sales turnover over $100 million, naming Charles & Keith, Osim and Breadtalk.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How about our bigger home-grown companies whose sales turnover are more than $100 million, like Charles & Keith, Osim, Breadtalk and many others?

sections.label: Rental rebates and outreach
sections.summary: Asks whether these companies will get rental rebates for their Singapore shops and whether Government has an outreach strategy.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will they be given rental rebates too for their shops in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Does the Government have a strategy to reach out to them to see what help these local companies require?

sections.label: Stricter dormitory requirements
sections.summary: Notes MOM's more stringent dormitory requirements, including no double decker beds and at least 6 m2 instead of 4.5 m2.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, more stringent dormitory requirements from MOM, which is expected because of the recent COVID-19 spread in the dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But suddenly, MOM said no double decker beds – each one must have at least 6 m2 instead of 4.5 m2 and so on.

sections.label: Levy waiver consent deadline
sections.summary: States that otherwise they will not get the levy waiver and consent must be given by 10 June.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Otherwise, they will not get the levy waiver.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And the consent must be given by 10 June.

sections.label: BCA project tiers
sections.summary: States BCA has given all projects tiers A, B, C and D, and contractors do not know their project's tier.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, for all the projects, BCA has given them tiers – tier A, tier B, tier C, tier D.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And the contractors do not know their project is in which tier.

sections.label: Swab testing cost
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government can absorb the swab testing cost beyond August.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can the Government absorb the swab testing cost beyond August?

sections.label: Workers levy waiver extension
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can extend the 100% workers levy waiver and $750 rebates until August, since most will not work until September or later.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, can the Government extend 100% workers levy waiver and $750 rebates till August since most of them will not be able to work until September or later?

sections.label: Property tax rebate for industrial buildings
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can extend the 30% property tax rebate to all industrial buildings and waive land rental until August.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government extend the 30% property tax rebate to all industrial buildings as most of the contractors occupy industrial buildings and waive the land rental till August?

sections.label: Supporting society to adapt to COVID-19
sections.summary: The passage states that measures should include training and time for those unused to smartphones, and that local businesses and contractors must be helped to stay afloat.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When we introduce these measures, we should give those who are not used to using smart phones sufficient training and time to adjust, including stallholders at coffee shops and hawkers at hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee, you have 30 seconds to wrap up your speech.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: We may have to live with COVID-19 for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: We must support everyone in our society to adapt to this new normal.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: So, we must help local businesses and contractors stay afloat.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Our businesses first and foremost want to get back to work, to stand on their own two feet.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Therefore, they hope the Government can be flexible in its requirements and listen more to their feedback.

sections.label: OCBC survey on wage cuts
sections.summary: The passage reports an OCBC survey finding wage cuts and job worries among working adults, and questions whether the retrenchment advisory protects against disguised retrenchments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In a recent survey conducted by OCBC on over 1,000 Singaporean and Permanent Resident working adults at about 1.5 months into the circuit breaker, about 55% reported experiencing some form of wage cut, reduction in commissioning earnings, wage freezing and being forced to convert to a part-time role, contractual instead of permanent role, or to take no-pay leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Almost half were worried about being retrenched or terminated within the next six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even though the “Advisory on retrenchment benefits payable to retrenched employees as a result of business difficulties due to COVID-19” issued on 20 May 2020 specify that “an employer who terminates an employment contract with no plan to fill the vacancy any time soon is presumed to have retrenched the employee,” it is unclear whether it goes far enough to protect employees from disguised retrenchments.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs places versus retrenchments
sections.summary: The passage states the 100,000 places in the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package may be less than the estimated number of retrenchments combined with job entrants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The current 100,000 places in SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package may or, in fact, is likely less than the estimated number of retrenchments as well if you combine them that job entrants such as fresh graduates entering the workforce.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget extends Job Support Scheme
sections.summary: The passage states that the Fortitude Budget extends the Job Support Scheme to businesses still unable to reopen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Fortitude Budget extends the Job Support Scheme to those businesses that are still unable to reopen.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme increase
sections.summary: Asks whether the Jobs Support Scheme could be raised to 75% for all firms up to August 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Due to how the circuit breaker pushed the pause button on most of our businesses and firms as well as how integrated our whole economy is even on a domestic level, would the Deputy Prime Minister and the relevant ministries consider increasing the Jobs Support Scheme to 75% for all firms and businesses up to and including August 2020?

sections.label: BCA approval delays clarified
sections.summary: On 3 June 2020, BCA and agencies clarified delays, simplified approval and estimated shorter approval periods for complete applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On 3 June 2020, BCA and the relevant agencies and Ministries clarified some of the delays, simplified the process to obtain approval, and estimated a shorter period for approval if the application is in order.

sections.label: Priority testing for renovation workers
sections.summary: Asks whether workers would be tested with priority so half-renovated homes can be completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given the homes are half-renovated and much disamenity is caused to the families, would there be priority given to test these workers so that the renovation can then be completed.

sections.label: Laptops for lower income students
sections.summary: Notes laptops procured for lower income students locally and warns of a digital gap nationally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In my constituency, we have procured laptops for students for lower income families to support their studies during the period of home-based learning, but on a national scale this is also very important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In an age of digitalisation and digital gadgets, we should be cautious about the exponentially wide gap this will create between children whose parents can afford the digital equipment and the children whose parents may not be able to afford.

sections.label: Tenants with low household income
sections.summary: States that many tenants under this scheme are Singaporeans with low household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A large number of tenants under this scheme are Singaporeans with low household income.

sections.label: Internet subscription rebate scheme
sections.summary: Suggests a rebate scheme for internet subscription fees to support low household income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In our country's preparation and effort to achieve the "Smart Nation" goal, I would like the government to consider my suggestion to introduce a rebate scheme to help in the payment of internet subscription fees to support Singaporeans with low household incomes so that they can continue to have a more stable and uninterrupted internet connection.

sections.label: Internet subscription fee rebate proposal
sections.summary: The proposal is to incorporate the internet subscription fee into the existing list of rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My proposal is to incorporate the internet subscription fee into the existing list of rebates.

sections.label: Budgets using national reserves
sections.summary: To date, three out of four budgets require the use of national reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To date, three out of four budgets require the use of national reserves.

sections.label: President's information on national reserves
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Deputy Prime Minister Heng explains whether the President was given information on national reserves for three budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such critical information is very crucial for the President make an evaluation in order to reach a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope Deputy Prime Minister Heng can explain whether the President has been given information about the amount available in the national reserves, when the Government presented the information and facts to support its request to obtain the President's consent, to use the national reserves for the three budgets, Solidarity, Resilience and Fortitude.

sections.label: Four budgets and $100 billion
sections.summary: Since the first Unity Budget 15 weeks ago, there are now four budgets with almost $100 billion committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since the first Unity Budget 15 weeks ago, we are now into our fourth Budget, almost one Budget per month and almost $100 billion committed to save lives and to save livelihoods.

sections.label: MNCs returning and donating JSS
sections.summary: Some MNCs decided they do not need the JSS and have returned and donated it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yes, some of the MNCs have already decided that they do not need the JSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: They have returned it, they have donated it.

sections.label: Spending saved money, not borrowing
sections.summary: The assurance is that even if accused of spending too much, the money is saved over the years, not borrowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What we can be assured of, and I have had a few video conferences with fellow legislators, friends from overseas, that even if we are accused of spending too much, we are not borrowing it, we are not spending money that is not ours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is money that we have saved over the years.

sections.label: Reassurance on crisis spending
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance to reassure the House and Singaporeans that not too much has been spent, and asks agencies to be gentle with citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the spirit of the song, I do urge the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance to reassure the House and Singaporeans that we really have not spent too much.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I believe that we can never do too much for our citizens during this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And as we project ahead, as the crisis continues – not just in Singapore but across the world – do we have enough?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also ask that our agencies take the gentlest possible touch with citizens during these unprecedented times in listening to those who feel that because of their circumstances, they have too little and will need much more.

sections.label: Groups facing difficulties
sections.summary: Members before the speaker raised examples including housing agents, car salesmen, F&B operators, casual workers, low-income families and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Many hon Members before me have raised examples like housing agents, car salesmen who have been facing difficulties over the years, F&B operators, casual workers, low-income families, persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Doing more for citizens
sections.summary: The speaker says we should not fear doing more for citizens, supports extending the Jobs Support Scheme and a $2.7 billion stimulus for jobs, traineeships and skills training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, let us not be afraid to do much more for our citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is never too late to do more and we can never have too little heart as we work to save lives and livelihoods in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In particular, the extension of the Jobs Support Scheme to affected businesses would certainly help businesses adjust to the loss of revenue during this period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also support the $2.7 billion stimulus to strengthen employment and to create more jobs, traineeships and skills training.

sections.label: Self-employed excluded from SIRS
sections.summary: The speaker highlights self-employed persons not eligible for the Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme because their trade income exceeded $100,000 or their home annual value exceeded $21,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Although the Solidarity Budget announced on 7 April 2020 had helped many businesses, the financial impact on many others who have not benefited from the budgetary provisions are felt deeply and keenly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I wish to highlight one group, and this would be persons who are self-employed but not eligible for the Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) due to the eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some of them had missed out because their trade income had exceeded $100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some had missed out because they reside in homes with an annual value of more than $21,000.

sections.label: Raising SIRS eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The speaker suggests raising the trade income criterion to $250,000 per annum and removing the home annual value criterion, and says those not needing help can return grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Consider raising the criteria of the trade income to $250,000 per annum and remove the criteria of the annual value of the homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In unprecedented times like this, the Government should try to assist as many people as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And for those who do not require any help from the Government, they can always be encouraged to return the grant or the subsidies back to the Government, which has already been done by many companies.

sections.label: Economic contraction and reorganisation
sections.summary: The speaker says there is now a window of opportunity to get organised, and the economy is expected to shrink by between 4% and 7% this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Instead, we now have a window of opportunity to get organised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This year, we expect the economy to shrink by between 4% and 7%.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills package
sections.summary: The Government aims to generate close to 100,000 opportunities through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package, compared with an average of 29,000 locals placed yearly in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government, as a whole, has declared our collective ambition – to generate close to 100,000 opportunities in jobs, traineeships or attachments and skills training through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To give Members a sense of scale, Workforce Singapore (WSG) and its partners like NTUC's e2i and MAS placed an average of 29,000 locals into jobs every year in the last three years – 29,000 as opposed to the 100,000 that we are aiming for between now and the end of the year.

sections.label: National Jobs Council national team
sections.summary: Senior Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam described the National Jobs Council as a national team to rally partners and build a pipeline of opportunities across sectors and skill levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Recognising the enormity of the task, Senior Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam has described the National Jobs Council (NJC) as a “national team” to rally and mobilise every possible partner to build up a pipeline of such opportunities, catering to multiple sectors and every skill level.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs initiative scaled up
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs initiative will be scaled up to provide more than 40,000 jobs in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Jobs initiative will be scaled up to provide more than 40,000 jobs in 2020.

sections.label: Traineeship pathways for graduates jobseekers
sections.summary: About 25,000 traineeship pathways are aimed at recent graduates and mid-career jobseekers, with over 1,000 organisations offering to host more than 11,000 traineeships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For a start, we aim to open up about 25,000 traineeship pathways for recent graduates and mid-career jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are heartened that more than 1,000 organisations, including many SMEs, have stepped forward to offer to host more than 11,000 traineeships.

sections.label: SGUnited Skills programme pathways
sections.summary: The SGUnited Skills programme aims to create up to 30,000 pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Skills programme aims to create up to 30,000 of such pathways.

sections.label: Air Transport reskilling and SBF partner
sections.summary: Close to 4,000 Air Transport workers will be reskilled for new roles, and the Singapore Business Federation signed up as main programme partner for the SGUnited Traineeships Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Close to 4,000 workers in the Air Transport sector will be reskilled for new roles, ready when our airhub opens in a much bigger way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Singapore Business Federation signed up to be our main programme partner for the SGUnited Traineeships Programme.

sections.label: Tripartism and new skills
sections.summary: Singapore knows the new skills needed for nearly every job role in Financial Services within three years, and tripartism lets all row together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In Financial Services, for example, we know the new skills needed within the next three years for practically every job role there is – that level of detail – every job role.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Third, and perhaps most important of all, Singapore's unique brand of tripartism means that even in stormy waters, we can row as one, in unison towards the same destination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Working together, we can clear roadblocks, widen existing pathways and open up new pathways where none existed.

sections.label: COVID-19 igniting Singapore unity
sections.summary: COVID-19 is a powerful virus that unleashed a worldwide storm but is igniting Singapore's unity, resilience, solidarity and fortitude.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: COVID-19 is a powerful virus that has unleashed a storm worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But for Singapore, it is igniting something quite remarkable – our unity, resilience, solidarity and fortitude.

sections.label: New schemes administered quickly
sections.summary: New schemes such as the TRF, COVID-19 Support Grant and Solidarity payments were administered in record short time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: New schemes, such as the TRF, COVID-19 Support Grant and Solidarity payments were administered in record short time.

sections.label: Van rental exceeds cash assistance
sections.summary: The monthly rental of the van he uses to transport tools already cost $1,700, exceeding the cash assistance he could receive in April or May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The monthly rental of the van he uses to transport tools alone already cost him $1,700, exceeding the cash assistance he could receive in April or May.

sections.label: Low interest for business loans
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether businesses could be helped with 0.1% low interest on existing business loans during deferment, similar to new ESG loans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Despite this, I can understand that there are implications on banks and therefore the entire system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But could we help these businesses by offering a 0.1% low interest to existing business loans in this deferment period, similar to new ESG loans?

sections.label: S$93 billion to combat pandemic
sections.summary: Within five months, the Government is pumping in S$93 billion just to combat the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Within a short span of five months, our Government is pumping in S$93 billion just to combat the pandemic.

sections.label: Relief per citizen comparison
sections.summary: Singapore's relief is S$23,225 per capita, topping the chart, while the United States is third at S$12,765 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: If we look at the relief per citizen or PR, Singapore tops the chart at S$23,225 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The United States – world superpower, world largest economy and worst hit by the pandemic – is third at S$12,765 per capita.

sections.label: Red line on reserves
sections.summary: The speaker asks how to moderate and whether a red line exists beyond which reserves should not be drawn further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Again, I want to ask how do we moderate ourselves and is there a red line beyond which we shall not draw further from our reserves?

sections.label: Investment commitments secured
sections.summary: Singapore secured about S$13 billion in investment commitments in the first half of this year for the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Despite our circumstances, Singapore secured about S$13 billion in investment commitments in the first half of this year for the "next few years".

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: These investments, in sectors including electronics and infocomm, will generate "a few thousand jobs" for workers in Singapore in the coming years.

sections.label: Window of opportunity estimate
sections.summary: The speaker estimates the window of opportunity at two to three years or maybe even faster.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Our people have to be ready fast and my own estimate of our window of opportunity would be two to three years or maybe even faster.

sections.label: Breakthrough and digital office
sections.summary: The speaker describes breaking through and rising from the ashes, and welcomes the SG Digital Office and 1,000 digital ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I will describe this as "涅槃重生，破茧成蝶" – to breakthrough and rise from the ashes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I also welcome the creation of SG Digital Office and 1,000 digital ambassadors.

sections.label: Digital conversion bonus proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Government might consider a digital conversion bonus for seniors in the very near future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: If we can leverage them more actively and allow them to earn an extra allowance, I believe we will see better results.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And since we are investing in digital capabilities, might the Government consider offering a "digital conversion bonus" for our seniors in the very near future?

sections.label: COVID-19 support and past reserves
sections.summary: The Government provided an average of $23,225 per person for COVID-19, drawing on past reserves due to fiscal prudence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Based on rough calculations, the Government has provided an average of $23,225 per person to cope with COVID-19, much higher than many other developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This demonstrated the Government's determination to help our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is the fiscal prudence by our past and present government that has enabled us to draw such a big sum of money from the past reserves to deal with this crisis.

sections.label: Returning money to reserves
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government will promise to return the money to the reserves when the economy improves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Will the Government promise to return the money to the reserves when the economy gets better and how is the Government going to fulfil this promise?

sections.label: Fortitude Budget and reserves
sections.summary: Without sufficient reserves, the $33 billion Fortitude Budget would not be possible, enabling four Budgets totaling $93 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If we do not have sufficient reserves, the $33 billion Fortitude Budget would not be possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because of this, we are able to come up with four Budgets totaling $93 billion to assist Singaporeans, save companies, save jobs and save lives.

sections.label: Pre-school staff COVID-19 infection rate
sections.summary: 14 pre-school staff have been diagnosed with COVID-19, an infection rate of 0.036%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Currently, 14 pre-school staff have been diagnosed with COVID-19, which translates to an infection rate of 0.036%.

sections.label: Estimated unaware infected local residents
sections.summary: Applying the pre-school staff infection rate to 2.4 million working citizens and PRs suggests 861 local residents may be infected unaware.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If we apply the testing and confirmed case numbers of the pre-school staff to the 2.4 million working citizens and Permanent Residents in Singapore, then the infection rate of 0.03% would mean that there may be 861 local residents who have been infected but are unaware about it.

sections.label: Digital Transformation Office and hawker bonus
sections.summary: Singapore has lagged in e-payments, so a Digital Transformation Office is established and hawkers get a $300 monthly bonus for five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, after so many years, we have lagged behind other Asian countries in terms of e-payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am happy to see the establishment of the Digital Transformation Office and that every hawker will be given a $300 monthly bonus for the next five years to encourage them to adopt cashless payments.

sections.label: IMDA platform focus suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests IMDA focus on one or two platforms such as PayNow and NETS to avoid confusing and distracting customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, this may lead to confusion and it may distract customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I suggest that IMDA focus on one or two platforms such as PayNow and NETS.

sections.label: Fourth Budget $93 billion
sections.summary: With this fourth Budget, the Government has pumped in $93 billion to help Singaporeans and the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: With this fourth Budget, the Government has already pumped in $93 billion to help Singaporeans and the economy.

sections.label: Funds for Jurong breakfasts
sections.summary: She raised about $20,000 through friends, Giving.sg and Loving Hearts Multi-Service Centre, funding about nine workers to provide 150 free breakfasts daily in Jurong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, she has raised about $20,000, not just from her friends, but also through the Giving.sg website and the Loving Hearts Multi-Service Centre in Jurong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These funds help to pay about nine workers, including her parents, to provide about 150 free breakfasts to families in Jurong every day.

sections.label: Pioneers and COVID-19 reserves
sections.summary: Like late 1960s and 1970s pioneers, we will be pioneers in winning the war over COVID-19, using reserves built up by our Pioneers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Like our pioneers in the late 1960s and 1970s that have built our nation from scratch, we will be the pioneers in winning the war over COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We are using the reserve build up by our Pioneers to fight the current crisis.

sections.label: SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeship Programme
sections.summary: The budget fortifies urgently needed support programmes, and the speech focuses on the SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeship Programme aiming to provide 4,000 traineeships for mid-career unemployed locals.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This budget is aptly-named because it seeks to fortify support programmes that are urgently needed across all levels of an economy beleaguered by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to focus my speech on the welcome support offered via the new SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeship Programme that aims to provide 4,000 traineeships for mid-career unemployed locals.

sections.label: Managing expectations and cross-training
sections.summary: Industry leaders recommend managing both sides' expectations for mutual understanding, and MOM should support employers across complementary companies to offer cross-training opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Principally, industry leaders recommend that expectations of both sides must be carefully managed to heighten mutual understanding and satisfaction with the programme.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOM should provide some flexibility and support for employers across a group of complementary companies to offer cross-training opportunities.

sections.label: Companies upfront on job prospects
sections.summary: Companies should tell trainees upfront about longer term job prospects and post-traineeship support.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Companies should also be upfront with their trainees about the potential for longer term job prospects or the lack thereof, and share in advance the kinds of post traineeship support they can provide.

sections.label: Technical and career preparatory training
sections.summary: The programme offers technical skills training in growth areas and career preparatory training such as branding and interview skills.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Besides providing training in technical skills relating to growth areas such as AI, cyber security and enterprise architecture, the programme also offers career preparatory training in areas such as professional branding, resume building and interview skills.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget focus on jobs
sections.summary: The central focus of the Fortitude Budget is jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The central focus of the Fortitude Budget is jobs.

sections.label: Support for young jobseekers
sections.summary: Young jobseekers get SGUnited Traineeship, Hiring Incentive and SGUnited Jobs support, and MOM will assist with advice and career counselling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As this group is young, we may not be as worried as we may be for older Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They will also receive support under the Fortitude Budget’s SGUnited Traineeship which aims to provide 21,000 traineeships for local first-time jobseekers, and there is additional support from the Hiring Incentive scheme which has been expanded to cover workers of all ages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Certainly, some of the 40,000 jobs to be created in the public and private sectors by the SGUnited Jobs initiative will be offered to this young cohort too.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, being young and with less experience, they may face obstacles searching for jobs in a very tight labour market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that MOM will take active steps to assist those who need advice and career counselling in applying for jobs and being matched with training programmes and jobs.

sections.label: Help repaying HDB loans
sections.summary: The speaker asks the government to help them with repayment of their HDB loans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I would like to ask the government to help them with the repayment of their HDB loans.

sections.label: Need for more home space
sections.summary: More home offices and home-based learning create demand for more space with internal dividers for family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: More and more people will need a home office and increasingly, home-based learning will be part of all students’ schedule, whether during emergencies, or, regularly utilised to ensure that the system is working and that the students and teachers stay familiar with the online learning platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Such a change in working and learning patterns means that there is a need and demand for a bit more space, with internal dividers, for all members of a family to do their jobs and studying sustainably, without disturbing one another.

sections.label: Government COVID-19 support and reserves
sections.summary: The Government has given $93 billion in support, creating the largest Budget deficit, and will draw up to $52 billion from reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our Government’s response has had no precedent – unstinting and rapid support to the tune of $93 billion thus far, resulting in the largest overall Budget deficit in our nation’s history.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Including this Budget, the Government will need to draw up to $52 billion dollars from its reserves.

sections.label: Caution on further reserve draws
sections.summary: With uncertain economic outlook and downside risks, the speaker supports setting aside $13 billion in Contingencies Funds but urges utmost prudence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the economic outlook remaining highly uncertain and with risks predominantly skewed to the downside, we should be very cautious when we do further draws on our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I support the call to set aside a sum of $13 billion in Contingencies Funds, but, I must urge the Government to do so with utmost prudence.

sections.label: Preparing workforce for post-COVID-19
sections.summary: The workforce must prepare for post-COVID-19 structural changes, and the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package creates 100,000 opportunities to mitigate unemployment risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We must prepare our workforce immediately for a post-COVID-19 environment, to adapt quickly to structural changes in the economy, changed consumer habits and new ways in which countries will compete and co-operate with one another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I also applaud Deputy Prime Minister for his bold move to launch the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, creating 100,000 opportunities in jobs, traineeships and skills training to mitigate risks associated with unemployment.

sections.label: Singapore investment commitments and safe harbor
sections.summary: Singapore secured $13 billion in investment commitments in four months, positioning itself as a safe harbor amid global instability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Amidst the doom and gloom, it is reassuring to learn that Singapore has secured $13 billion of investment commitments in just four months of this year – amongst the highest in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Indeed, as social, political and geopolitical instability continue to play out elsewhere in the world, Singapore is well positioned as the much-sought-after safe harbor for business, talent, intellectual property and investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I think many of us believed that Singaporeans were not attracted to care-giving jobs, so we were always going to be heavily reliant on foreign nurses and care-giving professionals.

sections.label: Temporary COVID-19 positions as opportunity
sections.summary: Temporary positions for COVID-19 have given people a chance to try this work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The large number of temporary positions made available to deal with COVID-19 has also provided a window of opportunity for people to try their hand at this work.

sections.label: Leveraging remote work for ICT growth
sections.summary: Remote work should be leveraged to boost Singapore's ICT sector, with companies supplementing local talent with global expertise beyond national borders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With working remotely accepted as the new normal, we should leverage this opportunity to supercharge Singapore's growth in the Infocomm Technology sector (ICT).

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the accelerated plan to build a strong pipeline of digital and technology skills locally as announced by Minister Iswaran yesterday, companies can also supplement the local talent pool with global expertise to scale the business by extending working from home beyond our national borders.

sections.label: Post-COVID work and innovation trends
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Emerging Stronger Task Force Committee to scrutinise work and innovation trends from the COVID-19 pandemic to inform recommendations for a post-COVID era.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our innovations in organising work and how work should be done, can fuel our ambition to be Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Emerging Stronger Task Force Committee to scrutinise these and other trends emerging from this COVID-19 pandemic, so that it may inform their recommendations to prepare Singaporeans for a post-COVID era.

sections.label: Support measures for pandemic groups
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes support measures: expanded COVID-19 Support Grant, SME rental waivers and installment repayments, and improved living conditions for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The support measures introduced will help ensure that we can all get through this pandemic and most importantly, get through it together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am thankful that the concerns of those on unpaid leave or reduced salaries have been addressed through expanding the COVID-19 Support Grant to help this group of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am thankful we are proposing to help the SMEs with further rental waivers and allow tenants to repay their arrears through installments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our migrant friends have worked hard to build, clean and maintain Singapore as the shining red dot we are today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad we have not left them behind and have committed to improving their living conditions.

sections.label: Insufficient childcare leave entitlement
sections.summary: The speaker states that current childcare leave entitlement is already insufficient in a regular year, leaving many parents with unpaid leave as the only option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As I have previously stressed, our current childcare leave entitlement is already insufficient during a regular year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The only option left for many parents is unpaid leave.

sections.label: Other countries' paid leave measures
sections.summary: The passage describes paid and job-protected leave measures for working parents introduced in the US, Canada, Italy and Belgium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the US, the Families First Coronavirus Response Act expands paid leave options for working parents who are unable to find childcare arrangements, entitling them up to 12 weeks of partially paid family leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Canada, working parents are entitled to job-protected leave of absence for up to 16 weeks under federal law, allowing parents to attend to childcare and eldercare needs while protecting them from being fired or penalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Italy, the government extended annual parental leave by 15 days for parents with children aged up to 12 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Belgium, the government introduced a special parental leave for parents of children under the age of 12 where parents can take leave in the form of 1/2 or 1/5 reduction of working time.

sections.label: Government-paid COVID-19 childcare leave proposal
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will consider introducing Government-paid COVID-19-related childcare leave at least until the end of Phase Two of re-opening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should; other countries have already done so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will consider introducing a Government-paid COVID-19-related childcare leave and provide it at least until the end of Phase Two of the re-opening after the circuit breaker.

sections.label: Rental arrears and rent waiver request
sections.summary: The speaker cites public rental household rent arrears figures and asks the Deputy Prime Minister to consider waiving six months' rent for rental flat households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MND shared that “about 5,200 public rental households, or about 10% of all public rental households, are in rent arrears”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Around one in four such households owes more than $3,000 in rent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister said in his Ministerial Statement last week, "Our path forward will be tough, but we will journey together".

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister if he could consider waiving six months’ rent for all households residing in rental flats, except for those whose rent is already covered under financial assistance from ComCare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For context, the Government is extending $334 million in rental relief for Government tenants in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A similar waiver for rental flat households would cost between $16 million and $57 million, based on my rough calculation.

sections.label: Budget cash flow support
sections.summary: Around $28 billion across four Budgets went to immediate cash flow needs and overheads, about a third of the total Budget to date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Across all four Budgets, around $28 billion has gone towards supporting immediate cash flow needs and overheads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is about a third of the total Budget to date.

sections.label: Moral hazard safeguards
sections.summary: Safeguards against moral hazard can include reducing dividends, restricting stock buybacks and requiring M&A activity to pay back support through clawback.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Safeguards against moral hazard can include: reducing dividends, restricting stock buybacks and requiring that any M&A activity should seek to pay back the support provided, that is, a clawback.

sections.label: Climate subsidies conditions
sections.summary: Subsidies and support to companies accelerating climate change should come with conditions for absolute emissions reductions enabling faster Paris Agreement commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Subsidies and support to companies accelerating climate change should come with conditions for absolute emissions reductions that enable us to accelerate our Paris Agreement commitments.

sections.label: Task Force representation request
sections.summary: A request for more diverse representation on the Task Force, realigning economic structures to put people first, and noting past prudence provided emergency funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can I please ask the Deputy Prime Minister to ensure a more diverse and better representation on this Task Force to secure a truly resilient and united future for Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our economic structures must be realigned to put people first so that we build back better as a well-being economy post-COVID.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will take our collective imagination, courage and collaboration to walk through this crisis and emerge stronger, together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us start the work for that to happen today with fortitude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Fortunately, past prudence has provided us with adequate emergency funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We are in the midst of a brutal war, the pandemic has claimed over 370,000 lives in the world within a few months.

sections.label: Wage support for upskilling
sections.summary: More salary or wage support can be given to help Singaporeans upskill or reskill without worrying about maintaining the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) and Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) provide welcomed relief, more salary or wage support can be given to help ease Singaporeans to upskill or reskill without having to worry about maintaining the family.

sections.label: JSS income cap appeal
sections.summary: Some appealed for the Job Support Scheme for working directors who are shareholders, asking why the $100,000 income cap is not removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some have appealed for the Job Support Scheme (JSS) for working directors who are also shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Instead of limiting the JSS to those who earn below $100,000 a year, why not remove this income cap?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: After all, the JSS is capped at 75% of $4,650.

sections.label: SMEs and hawkers challenges
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about challenges facing SMEs, micro-businesses and hawkers, and notes the Emerging Stronger Task Force studying COVID-19 shifts.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, as we chart our path forward, I am particularly concerned about the challenges faced by our SMEs, especially the micro-businesses in our neighbourhood and hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is encouraging that the Government has set up the Emerging Stronger Task Force to study the systemic shifts emerging out of COVID-19.

sections.label: Digital transformation estimates
sections.summary: Microsoft estimates two years of digital transformation occurred in two months, and Forbes estimates five years before mid 2021.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Microsoft estimates that two years of digital transformation was accomplished in the last two months.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Forbes estimates five years of digital transformation to occur before mid 2021.

sections.label: German seniors shopping online
sections.summary: With no local studies released, in 2019 40% of seniors aged 65 and above in Germany shopped online.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Although there are no local studies released, in 2019, 40% of seniors aged 65 and above in Germany shop online.

sections.label: Digital Ambassadors for hawkers, seniors
sections.summary: The SG Digital Office will hire 1,000 Digital Ambassadors to help hawkers and seniors learn digital skills.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: As we protect the lives of our seniors by social distancing, we should also take care of their quality of social life by using technology.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the SG Digital Office will be hiring 1,000 Digital Ambassadors to help hawkers and seniors learn digital skills.

sections.label: Flexible COVID-19 Support Grants
sections.summary: An MSF Senior Director conveyed that MSF would administer COVID-19 Support Grants flexibly, not just by closely adhering to criteria, to better serve the policy objective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As an example, I recently received a note from a Senior Director of MSF who conveyed to me that MSF would administer the COVID-19 Support Grants (CSG) flexibly and not just by closely adhering to the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This will ensure the policy objective of CSG of supporting lower to middle income Singaporeans who have lost their jobs, lost a significant proportion of the income or placed under no-pay leave are better served.

sections.label: Bill mandating rental waivers
sections.summary: The speaker is cheered by DPM Heng's announcement of a Bill mandating more muscular landlords to grant rental waivers to severely affected SME tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On the first point, I am cheered by Deputy Prime Minister Heng's announcement of the Government's decision to introduce a Bill, mandating the more muscular landlords to grant rental waivers to the SME tenants whose businesses have been severely affected because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Permanent framework for small businesses
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether Government intervention to help small businesses during crises should be temporary or a permanent framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At this point in time, given the severe impact of COVID-19 pandemic on small businesses, especially in the F&B and retail industries, I think it is right for Government to intervene to protect them or else they will disappear and the employees will be stranded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As it is well-known, two-third of Singaporeans are employed by SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The question I have is on whether we should take a temporary or permanent approach in dealing with such matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Now that the Government has recognised that there is a need for intervention to help small businesses during crises, should there not be a permanent framework that can be applied as and when the situation calls for it in the future?

sections.label: Permanent framework for rent issues
sections.summary: A permanent framework for rent issues faced by small businesses would make Singapore's economy more resilient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: By similarly having a permanent framework to deal with rent issues faced by the small businesses, we will be in effect making Singapore's economy more resilient.

sections.label: Dollar-for-dollar matching with outcomes
sections.summary: Speaker says Deputy Prime Minister Heng's dollar-for-dollar matching should be combined with an outcome driven approach for charity organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng's approach in providing dollar-for-dollar matching addresses both concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In my respectful view, however, the dollar-for-dollar matching should be combined with an outcome driven approach so as to incentivise charity organisations to collaborate and delivery quality programmes for Singaporeans in need.

sections.label: Home equity loans for families
sections.summary: Speaker asks if Government could nudge financial institutions to provide low-interest home equity loan facilities for asset-rich, cash-poor families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our Government has taken decisive steps to ensure that banks better support individuals and businesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What I fear though is that if the economy dwindles even further, more families, especially middle-income families who are not the primary targets of the care and support package, will find themselves more cash strapped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We all recognise that there is a limit to payments such as the Solidarity Payment or the Temporary Relief Fund that the Government may make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
