sentences.text: For these asset-rich, cash-poor families, I wonder if the Government could consider nudging the financial institutions to provide hassle-free, low-interest home equity loan facilities secured by either (a) refinancing of the original mortgage facilities if the original mortgagee is a bank; or (b) by a second mortgage on their homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To my understanding, such options are not currently available for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Traditionally, financial institutions are chary about being second mortgagees as, priority-wise, they rank below CPF and the first mortgagee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The administration costs in terms of getting valuation and to draw up legal paperwork can be significant too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I appreciate that this measure has to be carefully studied for its social impact because if families default on their obligations, the banks may have to foreclose on their homes.

sections.label: Four Budgets in four months
sections.summary: There have been an unprecedented four Budgets in a period of less than four months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To that, we have an unprecedented four Budgets in a short period of less than four months.

sections.label: JSS support and rental cash grant
sections.summary: Fortitude Budget continues wage supplements for selected industries, gives most businesses up to 25%, and provides a cash grant to offset SME rental costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the past two months, under the circuit breaker period, businesses have received support under the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), limited to 75% or up to $4,600 of every salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under this Fortitude Budget, for the months ahead, only selected industries such as listed in Tiers 1 and 2 of the JSS will continue to receive wage supplements of up to 75% of each worker's salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For most businesses, they will only be receiving up to 25% of the first $4,600 of every worker's salary for the remaining payments under the JSS, and this Fortitude Budget will only bring one additional month's payment, limited to 25% of an employee's salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has announced that it will provide a cash grant to offset rental costs of SME tenants and also pass a new law to ensure landlords pass on rental support from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will be welcomed as a small temporary relief of 0.64 of a month's rental for office and industrial properties and 0.8 of a month's rental for commercial properties.

sections.label: Chan Chun Sing workplace return caveats
sections.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing said only workers needing machinery, terminals or legal documentation can return to workplaces, with others working from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Chan Chun Sing was reported in the media on 19 May to have said as follows, "Only those who require the use of machinery and specialised terminals or need to complete legal documentation will be able to return to their workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The rest of the workers will continue to work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will allow more than three-quarters of our economy to resume their normal operations." These caveats are a challenge to viable resumption for many businesses.

sections.label: Projected number of released workers
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Minister can project how many workers will be released back to work in each of the next two to three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Further, is the Minister able to give a projected estimation of the number of these workers who will be released back to work in each of the next two to three months?

sections.label: Singapore-China fast lane air travel
sections.summary: The Government announced plans for a fast lane arrangement with COVID-19 measures for essential business and official air travel between Singapore and China in early June, starting with six Chinese cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last Friday, the Government announced plans to launch "fast lane" arrangement with COVID-19 measures for essential business, official air travel between Singapore and China in early June, starting with six Chinese cities.

sections.label: Khaw Boon Wan transport and reserves
sections.summary: Minister Khaw Boon Wan said rail and bus services will return to pre-circuit breaker levels but safe social distancing may not be possible, and questions were raised about reserves and wage support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan announced on Monday that rail and bus services will return to pre-circuit breaker levels but indicated that safe social distancing may not be possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is also inconsistent with the stringent enforcement efforts adopted in many other situations with regards to social distancing, for which many people have been fined or given warnings for breaches and the rationale for such enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I wonder whether the President, in arriving at her conclusion to support the draw of $31 billion from our reserves as well as the previous draws from reserves under the previous Budgets, had already been advised of the total amount of reserves Singapore has and had taken this into consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: After May, most businesses will receive 25% wage support and the Fortitude Budget will only increase support by one more month of such wage support.

sections.label: Social distancing on public transport
sections.summary: The relaxation of social distancing on trains is a concern, inconsistent with enforcement elsewhere, and questions were raised about the President's advice on reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The relaxation of social distancing in our trains since Tuesday is a huge concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lack of social distancing on public transport is inconsistent with the authorities’ stringent enforcement efforts in social distancing elsewhere, not to mention a potential Achilles heel in our fight against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I wonder whether the President, in arriving at her conclusion to support the draw of $31 billion from our reserves as well as the previous draws from reserves under the Solidarity and Resilience Budgets, had already been advised of the total amount of reserves Singapore has and had taken this into consideration.

sections.label: NAC support for artists
sections.summary: As at 22 May 2020, NAC supported more than 850 artists and arts groups, funded over 60 digitalisation projects and reached over 6.2 million online views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As at 22 May 2020, NAC has supported more than 850 artists and arts groups, funded more than 60 digitalisation projects and reached over 6.2 million online views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we take into consideration of the other online digital programmes by the arts groups, we should reach more than 10 million online viewers as today.

sections.label: Arts support under Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: The $55 million Arts and Culture Resilience Package supports arts organisations and practitioners until year-end and encourages longer-term capabilities after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the artists and arts groups can tap on the Fortitude Budget to sustain works, spread positivity and make arts as an essential for everyone in the new normalcy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They can explore and tap on the Enhanced Jobs Support Scheme, SEP Income Relief Scheme, COVID-19 Support Grant and the Arts and Culture Resilience Package (ACRP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The $55 million ACRP seeks to protect the arts and culture eco-system and will provide support and opportunities for our cultural organisations and practitioners until the end of the year, while encouraging the development of longer-term capabilities that will help the community emerge stronger after COVID-19.

sections.label: Digital arts online viewership
sections.summary: Advanced digital technologies bring arts to social media platforms, with more than 10 million online viewership to-date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They use advanced digital technologies to bring arts onto various social media platforms, so that their audiences can enjoy wonderful concerts and performances free at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are more than 10 million online viewership to-date.

sections.label: Support for Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: The speaker states support for the Fortitude Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): I am in support of the Fortitude Budget.

sections.label: Finely calibrated COVID-19 rules confusion
sections.summary: Rules since early April were often qualified or changed after announcement, causing confusion, as with outlet-based confectionery suspensions on 21 April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In hindsight, though, many Singaporeans, looking back on the rules and announcements issued since early April, would say that there were too many finely calibrated rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These were often qualified or changed shortly after being announced and this led to confusion on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On 21 April, when the tighter circuit breaker measures were announced, the press release said outlet-based confectionery operations had to be suspended from 2359 hours on 21 April, but those selling mainly bread could continue.

sections.label: Essential and non-essential company categories
sections.summary: The Government's approach to Phase One and beyond hinges on demarcating companies as essential or non-essential for each phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government's approach to Phase One and beyond hinges on demarcating companies into either an essential or non-essential category for each phase.

sections.label: Alternative broader calibration approach
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government considered calibrating less finely and with a broader brush.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Has the Government considered an alternative approach which is to calibrate this a little less finely and with a broader brush.

sections.label: PCR test result time
sections.summary: Scaling up the current PCR test is challenged because results take about three hours to obtain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Some challenges of scaling up the current PCR test are that testing takes about three hours for results to be obtained.

sections.label: Scaling up other testing methods
sections.summary: Given difficulties scaling up PCR testing, other testing methods must be explored concurrently to roll out effective mass testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Given the challenges in scaling up the PCR testing method, there is a need to concurrently explore scaling up of other testing methods to be able to roll out effective mass testing.

sections.label: Utilities rebate in Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: The latest Fortitude Budget includes a $100 utilities rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, there is a $100 utilities rebate in this latest Fortitude Budget – $100.

sections.label: Foreign direct investment commitments
sections.summary: Minister Chan announced $13 billion in foreign direct investment commitments in the first four months of this year, versus $15.2 billion for all of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Chan recently announced $13 billion in foreign direct investment commitments in the first four months of this year versus $15.2 billion for the whole of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How many jobs is this expected to be translated into?

sections.label: Learning from other countries' COVID-19 success
sections.summary: Other developed countries' COVID-19 success should give Singapore pause to learn, including on early reusable mask wearing and balancing state and non-state sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The success achieved by other developed countries in the region against COVID-19 such as Taiwan, Korea, Hong Kong and New Zealand should give us pause that we, too, have things to learn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, if stronger independent voices had come out to say the precautionary reusable mask wearing was okay in the early days, it may have cut down on some asymptomatic transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last year, I read an excellent book called "The Narrow Corridor" by academics Daron Acemoglu and James Robinson.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It uses extensive historical research spanning centuries to argue that the most successful societies are those that find the right balance between a strong, capable state and an equally strong non-state sector – meaning civil society, alternative parties and the private sector – to balance that state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The outcomes of such successful societies are able to obtain combined political stability and law and order on the one hand together with long-term innovation-driven economic development and social progress on the other hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singaporeans bear a major two-fold responsibility to preserve what is good about our existing system but to change what should be changed to make it better.

sections.label: Growth forecast downward adjustment
sections.summary: On the day the Deputy Prime Minister delivered this Budget, MTI announced a downward adjustment of the growth forecast from -1% to -4%, to -4% to -7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the day the Deputy Prime Minister delivered this Budget, MTI announced a downward adjustment of our growth forecast of -1% to -4%, to -4% to -7%.

sections.label: JSS expiry and retrenchments
sections.summary: The passage states that as JSS expires in time, some retrenchments are inevitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As JSS expires in time, some retrenchments are inevitable.

sections.label: SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeships openings
sections.summary: The passage states the 4,000 openings may not appear large next to the Singaporean workforce but are an important source of hope for Singaporeans who lost or will lose jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On jobs, Mr Speaker, the headline numbers vis-a-vis initiatives like the new SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeships scheme of 4,000 openings may not appear large next to the size of the Singaporean workforce, but they are an important source of hope for those Singaporeans who have lost their jobs or will lose their jobs.

sections.label: Contingencies Fund in Budget
sections.summary: The passage states the employment of the Contingencies Fund in this Budget answered the question posed during the Resilience Budget debate speech about whether the next Government would have enough fiscal firepower for the COVID-19 fallout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, the employment of the Contingencies Fund in this Budget answered the question posed during my Resilience Budget debate speech, which queried whether the next Government would have enough fiscal firepower to deal with the effects of the COVID-19 fallout.

sections.label: Deputy Prime Minister on financial position
sections.summary: The passage states the Deputy Prime Minister was quoted in the media after the Fortitude Budget saying Singapore's financial position will be a lot weaker in the coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After delivering the Fortitude Budget, the Deputy Prime Minister was also quoted in the media as saying that Singapore's financial position will be a lot weaker in the coming years.

sections.label: Official COVID-19 communication and confusion
sections.summary: The passage states straight talk on Singapore's limitations and shortcomings did not always define official Government communication on COVID-19, and describes perceptions of confusion over piecemeal announcements, u-turns and positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, straight talk, especially on Singapore's limitations and shortcomings in managing the crisis, did not always define official Government communication on COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There was a perception among some Singaporeans of a public confused with many piecemeal announcements, u-turns and positions that did not gel intuitively, like limiting the number of visits to parents and grandparents to two individuals, when public transport safe distancing rules had already been lifted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Other Members have spoken about the operational frustrations of businesses, like those in construction, and I will not repeat these.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This morning, the Straits Times carried a story on COVID-19 regulations comparing hair treatments that go on for hours, contrasted with directives that prohibit beauty treatments that last more than 30 minutes.

sections.label: Malaysia border closure and crisis preparedness
sections.summary: The passage states Malaysia closed its borders before the circuit breaker, causing difficult adjustment for Singaporean companies reliant on foreign labour, and that gaps like lack of understanding of DORSCON need plugging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Malaysia closed its borders before our circuit breaker, resulting in a difficult adjustment for many Singaporean companies, both public and private, reliant on foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Public crisis preparedness, such as a lack of understanding of emergency terminology like DORSCON also revealed gaps that need to be plugged in future.

sections.label: Economic self-sufficiency and essential sectors
sections.summary: Calls for taking stock of the economy and relooking at sectors needing greater self-sufficiency and buffer, especially essential jobs and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, and critically, we must take stock of the entire economy and relook at sectors where greater self-sufficiency and buffer are required, especially essential jobs and services.

sections.label: Foreign worker accommodation and culture
sections.summary: Calls the Government's quick introduction of foreign worker accommodation guidelines and promotion of respectful culture a positive development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the Government's decision to quickly introduce guidelines for better foreign worker accommodation standards and the promotion of a more respectful culture between Singaporeans and migrant workers has been a very positive development.

sections.label: Citizen engagement and COVID-19 opportunity
sections.summary: Urges more avenues for citizen engagement and data sharing, and says COVID-19 is an opportunity to build a better Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moving forward, the Government should look at opening more avenues like Parliament for citizen engagement, greater data sharing and empower other institutions like our think-tanks, and nudge the mainstream media to give alternative perspectives more voice and even provide platforms piloting change on a small scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As many Singaporeans will have to buckle down to take on new skills and jobs, COVID-19 has also provided an opportunity for Singaporeans to take a deeper interest in their country and their society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a positive development, even as COVID-19 has hit Singapore while we contend with other pressing short and medium term issues, such as demographic shifts, technological disruption, climate change and, more ominously, the impact to our position as a global Asia hub from US-China competition and rivalry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The economic picture may be bleak today and, for some, a moment of anguish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But as I had put forth in my response to the Resilience Budget, there are opportunities to reset some fundamental assumptions about the type of society we can endeavour and pivot towards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The transition will demand everyone's participation, effort and energies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But with the people determined and committed to the nation's recovery and success, COVID-19 is a golden opportunity for this generation to envision and build a better Singapore.

sections.label: Merchant e-commerce challenges survey
sections.summary: A May 2020 survey of 48 merchant associations found capabilities and cost were the top challenges merchants face in digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A survey of 48 merchant associations representing almost 500 merchants was conducted in May 2020 by the Federation of Merchant Association Singapore's heartland enterprises unit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When the merchants were asked what challenges they face in joining the e-commerce wagon, as they put it, about half of the respondents quoted these two top challenges: one, the lack of their own internal capabilities to sustain the digitalisation efforts; and two, the cost of implementation and the recurring costs of digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Capabilities and cost, not only during adoption, but also in sustaining the efforts, remain their top concerns.

sections.label: Charity fundraising matching cap
sections.summary: Suggests raising the $250,000 cap in the Enhanced Fundraising Programme to incentivise more donors to give now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister shared that in the years ahead, a "stronger social service sector will be even more critical".

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I want to also thank Deputy Prime Minister for including the charities and SSAs in the Fortitude Budget in many schemes, such as Job Support Scheme and the Enhanced Fundraising Programme to match donations up to $250,000 per charity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Suggestion one: raise the cap of $250,000 in the Enhanced Fundraising Programme for larger charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For such a time as this, fundraising is expectedly very challenging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is hence useful for Government to consider raising the matching amount in order to incentivise more donors to invest now, rather than later or never.

sections.label: Severely disabled and low-income groups
sections.summary: Lists groups served, including the severely disabled, autism day activity centre beneficiaries, residential home residents, rare disorder families and lower income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Some are the more severely disabled groups, such as beneficiaries in the autism day activity centres where we serve the more severe ones, residential homes, such as that run by St Andrew's, families with rare disorders are kids with rare disorders and multiple disabilities and lower income households sandwiched by elderly and younger disabled.

sections.label: Disability jobs chapter proposal
sections.summary: A speaker urges setting up a National Jobs Council chapter for employability training and employment of the disabled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, that is four – include the people sector including the vulnerable, the disabled; right at the start in the planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And suggestion five: the last one for this group, is to start a disability chapter in the National Jobs Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Commissioned by MSF Minister, Mr Desmond Lee, a workgroup that is led by Minister of State Sam Tan and myself is working on the underlying factors for this issue and a report will be published by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 outbreak, however, adds urgency to the challenges faced by the disability community especially in the areas of digitalisation and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I therefore urge Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance Heng and Senior Minister Tharman to set up a chapter in the National Jobs Council for the employability training and employment for the disabled so that they will not fall further behind.

sections.label: JSS support for businesses
sections.summary: The JSS scheme supports businesses unable to resume after circuit breaker with 75% of monthly wages till August.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current JSS scheme supports businesses that are unable to resume when a circuit breaker ends, with 75% of monthly wages till August or until they open.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Again, it will receive 25% of Monday wages being in JSS Tier 3.

sections.label: Outdoor sporting facilities reopening
sections.summary: When Phase Two comes, outdoor sporting facilities can open again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When Phase Two comes, outdoor sporting facilities can open again.

sections.label: Enterprise innovation grant for sport
sections.summary: The Enterprise Innovation and Capability Development Grant supports businesses with innovative and smart solutions in the sport industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For those that can find a way to digitise, the Enterprise Innovation and Capability Development Grant was announced a week ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This grant supports businesses that can come out with innovative and smart solutions within the sport industry.

sections.label: More sports in curriculum
sections.summary: More emphasis needs to be placed on sports, making it a bigger part of the curriculum from kindergarten through Junior College and Polytechnic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More emphasis needs to be placed on sports in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must create an environment where sports is a bigger part of the curriculum from kindergarten all the way through Junior College and Polytechnic.

sections.label: Stronger sporting industry
sections.summary: For the sporting industry to be sustainable, a stronger industry with more opportunities must be created.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the sporting industry to be sustainable in Singapore, we must create a stronger industry with more opportunities.

sections.label: Opening public sector facilities to industry
sections.summary: The passage proposes giving companies access to public sector facilities and support for workforce upskilling, hiring, curriculum development and new markets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One of the ways is to provide them access to the many facilities that we have developed over the years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have many facilities that are largely reserved for use only by the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Opening up access would create more opportunities for the industry to grow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For these companies, we could offer support for growth, examples include upskilling of workforce, hiring of middle aged educators who are looking for a career switch, support for programme or curriculum development and support for new market development.

sections.label: Accessible formats for deaf and disabled
sections.summary: The passage calls for public materials in Easy Read, large print, braille and deafblind formats because sign language is the first language for many deaf people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is important because that is the first language for many people who are deaf.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need public materials that can be converted into "Easy Read" format so that they can be accessible for people with cognitive impairment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to develop accessible written information products by using appropriate document formats with structured headings, large print, braille versions and formats for people who are deafblind or visually impaired.

sections.label: Priority shopping and delivery slots
sections.summary: The passage says priority shopping hours should include invisible disabilities and proposes priority delivery slots for persons with disabilities staying home with compromised immune systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The priority shopping hour for vulnerable groups is a great start and we hope that persons with all disabilities can access this, including those with invisible disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some PWDs find it difficult to go to supermarkets because they are staying at home due to having compromised immune systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, other than a priority shopping hour, introducing priority delivery slots will also help.

sections.label: Assistive Technology Fund reimbursement limits
sections.summary: The passage states the Assistive Technology Fund is a means-tested reimbursement fund taking up to three weeks, which may not suit those struggling financially.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While there is an existing Assistive Technology Fund for Persons with Disabilities, it is a reimbursement fund tied to means testing and the reimbursement can also take up to three weeks which may not be a feasible option for those who are struggling financially.

sections.label: SIRS eligibility and COVID-19 disability touchpoint
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SIRS amounts, duration and eligibility can be extended for persons with disabilities and calls for a disability touchpoint for COVID-19 response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, some PWDs rely on informal and temporary work arrangements and as such, do not strictly fit into the eligibility requirements of SIRS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taking that into consideration, can the Government consider extending the amount that is given and the duration of the relief for persons with disabilities or increasing the eligibility to those with higher household incomes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, it is important to have a disability touch point for the COVID-19 response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Having a touch point within the Government or related agencies where persons with disabilities, their care-givers and organisations can feedback on the accessibility of COVID-19 response information and measures is key.

sections.label: Global mask supply constraints
sections.summary: The passage states that supply constraints were global and some economies banned mask exports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Chee Hong Tat, I believe you have a clarification.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We explained to the public that there were supply constraints globally and some economies have in fact banned the export of masks.

sections.label: Face shields versus full-face masks
sections.summary: Face shields leave gaps around the face, so people were encouraged to use full-face masks instead as community and economy reopened.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Given that face shields do not provide a full coverage of your face, your nose and your mouth because there are gaps between the shield and your face, it poses certain risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These risks are less of a concern during the circuit breaker period when most people are asked to stay home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: But when we open up the community and the economy, we expect more interaction and therefore, we need to enhance the protection where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Therefore, we encouraged people to use the full-face mask instead of a face shield.

sections.label: Face shields for teaching
sections.summary: Face shields are allowed for teaching, but in other circumstances a mask is required.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We have therefore allowed face shields to be used for teaching.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: But in other circumstances, we will require a mask to be used.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme and rental waivers
sections.summary: The Government introduced the Jobs Support Scheme, waived or gave rebates on manpower levies, and proposed legislation mandating commercial landlords to grant rental waivers to SME tenants hit by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To support manpower cost and to save jobs, the Government has introduced the Jobs Support Scheme and either waived or provided rebates on manpower levies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More significantly, this is now being reinforced with proposed legislation to mandate commercial landlords to grant rental waivers to their SME tenants who have suffered a reduction in businesses due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is rare in Singapore's context as the Government does not usually engage in direct intervention of the market, especially in private business arrangements.

sections.label: Home-based learning participation
sections.summary: Since the circuit breaker began, school-going children of all ages adopted home-based learning, with over 96% of students reported participating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Since the start of the circuit breaker, school-going children across all age groups have adopted home-based learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was reported that more than 96% of students are participating in it.

sections.label: Digital learning device accessibility gap
sections.summary: The figures suggest a gap in digital learning accessibility, and MOE intends to accelerate device ownership for Secondary students from 2028, with questions on other levels and device type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These figures suggest that there is a gap in accessibility to digital learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that MOE intends to accelerate the ownership of digital learning devices for all Secondary school children from their initial date of 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I would like to clarify if there are similar plans to accelerate the ownership of these devices for children from other levels of study – so not just Secondary school students and above, but perhaps for Primary school students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And more critically, if there are, will this device be purchased off-the-shelf and supplied by different tech companies or will it be a proprietary device uniquely designed and manufactured by MOE for our schools and for our school children?

sections.label: Tiered personal learning device ownership
sections.summary: Tiering device ownership cost by household income could meet environmental and smart nation goals so no school-going child is deprived of a personal learning device.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This would meet the twin goals of being environmentally friendly while also taking a huge step towards being a digital smart nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We could tier the ownership cost of the device depending on varying household incomes, with the aim that no school-going child should be deprived of their own personal learning device.

sections.label: Neutral Smart Learning device branding
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to consider neutral branding for personal Smart Learning devices to encourage status equality and standard upgrades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The deliberately neutral branding also encourages status equality, not to mention standard software and hardware upgrades that will leave no child lacking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I urge the MOE to give this idea a serious thought and I look forward to the day that not only can we ensure that every student – every student is provided with their own personal Smart Learning device, but we can take pride that this device was designed and produced by our MOE, specially for our children.

sections.label: Support for Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: The speaker concludes in support of the Fortitude Budget, expecting a stronger society after COVID-19, and notes construction work was suspended during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the Government playing a pivotal role and strengthening its commitment to the people, I am certain that we will emerge as a stronger and more cohesive society after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I thus conclude my speech in firm support of the Fortitude Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: During the circuit breaker period, most construction work was suspended.

sections.label: COVID-19 cases among construction workers
sections.summary: The vast majority of COVID-19 cases have been amongst construction workers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The vast majority of our COVID-19 cases have been amongst construction workers.

sections.label: First tranche projects restart
sections.summary: The first tranche of projects could not be left idle for safety reasons and were allowed to restart from 2 June.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We had the first tranche of projects which could not be left idle for long because of safety reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These have been allowed to restart from 2 June.

sections.label: Cleared dormitories announced
sections.summary: MOM announced the first batch of 60 cleared dormitories, with another 111 due to be cleared in coming weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Earlier this week, MOM announced the first batch of 60 cleared dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And another 111 are due to be cleared in the coming weeks.

sections.label: BCA as construction restart point agency
sections.summary: BCA will be the point agency and one stop-shop for all matters regarding construction restart to avoid confusion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To avoid the situation where companies do not know who to approach for information, BCA will be the point agency in Government or the one stop-shop front for all matters regarding construction restart.

sections.label: Construction sector job support
sections.summary: Construction firms and consultancy firms get higher 75% JSS support for June to August wages, plus foreign worker levy waivers and rebates until July.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister announced during the Fortitude Budget speech that the construction sector will receive enhanced support under the job support scheme until August.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And let me assure Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that similar to construction firms, the consultancy firms will also be eligible for the higher tier of 75% JSS support for wages paid between June and August this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In addition, companies whose foreign workers are not able to resume work will receive foreign worker levy waivers and rebates until July.

sections.label: Government bears testing costs
sections.summary: In the short term the Government will help bear additional costs, including paying for workers' testing costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In the short term, the Government will help to bear the additional costs, including paying for the testing costs for workers.

sections.label: BCA one-stop approval platform
sections.summary: BCA has set up a one-stop platform to facilitate such approvals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: BCA has since set up a one-stop platform to facilitate such approvals.

sections.label: Coordinating agencies to resume construction
sections.summary: The Government will coordinate agencies, share information and work with industry associations to resume construction and transform the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will coordinate amongst various agencies and lean forward to provide information to you and work closely with your industry associations and with you to resume construction as soon as we can and work together to transform our sector in the medium to long term.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And I am very heartened to hear the strong support that the Minister just mentioned given to the construction industry.

sections.label: Collective responsibility for fiscal health
sections.summary: Parliamentarians are collectively responsible for the nation's fiscal health, which allows drawing on reserves and tabling four Budgets in four months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As parliamentarians, we are collectively responsible for our nation's fiscal health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is the reason why we are able to draw on our reserves and table an unprecedented four Budgets in four months.

sections.label: Drawing on past reserves
sections.summary: Facing a deep and prolonged recession, the House drew S$4.9 billion from past reserves, over 10 times more than in 2009.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, how long do we expect this to last?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then, when faced with a fast deteriorating global economic environment and the prospect of a deep and prolonged recession, the House drew down on S$4.9 billion from past reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, Sir, we are drawing over 10 times more than what we drew in 2009.

sections.label: Returning drawn reserves
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister is asked to share plans to return money drawn from reserves in coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Deputy Prime Minister share his plans to return the money drawn back to our reserves in the years to come?

sections.label: Four-day work week proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes moving from a five-day to a four-day work week with work-from-home and flexi-hours options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, as we reopen the economy, we have to fundamentally rethink future job arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose moving away from the traditional five-day work week to a four-day work week with the option of working from home on the fifth day and even having a flexi-hours work model.

sections.label: Digital inclusion for rental flats
sections.summary: The speaker urges MCI and IMDA to distribute internet devices and affordable wifi to rental flat residents, and commends Seniors Go Digital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singaporeans living in rental flats and those in the lower income brackets are disproportionately less likely to have wifi at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, in the last three months, we have seen regular media coverage about the struggles that some of these families face trying to ensure that their children can participate in home-based learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The existing Digital Inclusion framework needs to be reinforced so that no one gets left behind causing a digital divide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge MCI and IMDA to redouble their efforts in distributing internet connected devices, and work to ensure that affordable wifi is available to residents living in our rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to express my support and commend MCI and IMDA for launching the Seniors Go Digital Movement.

sections.label: Payroll support and rental waivers
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme extension gives employers up to 75% payroll support to August, and rental waivers of two to four months are shared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to payroll, the extension of the Jobs Support Scheme means that many employers, particularly those in troubled sectors like aviation, will continue to get significant payroll support for their staff, up to 75% through to August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Rental waivers of two to four months will be enjoyed by many businesses, the load shared between landlords and the Government.

sections.label: Income loss relief and reserves draw
sections.summary: Those losing 30% or more income get relief, Care and Support payments continue, 100,000 jobs are planned, and about $50 billion is drawn from reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Whether you are self-employed or an employee, if you have lost 30% or more of your income, there will be relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In addition to this, payments to families from Care and Support packages in previous Budgets will continue and this will help households meet expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is also significant investment in job creation and training opportunities, with a bold plan to create 100,000 jobs and the team is already in place headed by Senior Minister Tharman to look into this very difficult project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: All this spending comes with a price tag, and in this case, we will, for the first time in our history, be dipping into our reserves to the tune of around $50 billion.

sections.label: Justifying $50 billion draw-down
sections.summary: A one-off $50 billion draw-down is called probably justified, noting reserves are the Golden Goose and the last draw was in 2008/2009.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, a one off draw-down of $50 billion to deal with what is probably the biggest financial crisis since our Independence is probably justified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We must however be mindful that these reserves built up since our Independence are our “Golden Goose”, and the more we spend of the reserves, the less the net investment income will be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The last time we drew down on these reserves was during the 2008/2009 Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: Singapore COVID-19 support measures
sections.summary: Singapore's low COVID-19 death rate is cited alongside business and individual financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Although we have a large number of cases, because we have managed the situation, our death rate from COVID-19 is one of the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For those who own businesses, there is support for payroll, relief from rental and financing available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For individuals who have lost jobs and income, there is financial assistance available as well as training to get new jobs.

sections.label: WHO coronavirus global impact estimates
sections.summary: WHO estimates the coronavirus infected 6.4 million, claimed over 380,000 lives and closed borders worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Within six months, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that the coronavirus has infected 6.4 million people, claimed over 380,000 lives, disrupted lives and livelihoods, and closed borders worldwide.

sections.label: IMF global economy contraction projection
sections.summary: The IMF projects the global economy to contract sharply by 3 percentage points, worse than the global financial crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects the global economy to contract sharply by 3 percentage points.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is much worse than the 0.07% contraction during the global financial crisis and is unseen since the Great Depression.

sections.label: Economy reopening by end June
sections.summary: Large parts of the economy are expected to reopen by end June if infection rates stay low and stable.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: If infection rates remain low and stable, we expect large parts of the economy to be able to reopen by the end of June.

sections.label: Singapore-China fast lane borders
sections.summary: The Singapore-China fast lane is described as a first step in reopening borders.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Singapore-China "fast lane" is a first step in this reopening of borders.

sections.label: Singapore COVID-19 response spending
sections.summary: Singapore commits almost $100 billion, close to 20% of GDP, with four Budgets totalling $193 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We, too, have mounted a strong response because lives and livelihoods are at stake.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are committing almost $100 billion, or close to 20% of our GDP, to our COVID-19 response.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Adding the COVID-19 response to our usual spending, the total size of our four Budgets stands at $193 billion.

sections.label: COVID-19 response worker business support
sections.summary: Over $72 billion, close to 80% of the COVID-19 response amount, is committed to helping workers stay in jobs and supporting businesses and employees.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By investing in upgrading the skills of our people and transforming our businesses, the economy can recover more strongly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is why over $72 billion, or close to 80% of the amount set aside for the COVID-19 response, is committed to helping our workers stay in their jobs, and supporting our businesses and their employees, which, in turn, support social resilience.

sections.label: COVID-19 unemployment impact
sections.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic is expected to be more severe than SARS, with unemployed residents potentially rising from around 73,000 in 2019 to above 100,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic is widely expected to be more severe than SARS, with the number of unemployed residents potentially rising from around 73,000 in 2019 to above 100,000 in 2020.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills package
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills package seeks to grow pathways to jobs and equip workers and firms with capabilities for coming years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills package seeks to not only grow pathways to jobs, but also equip workers and their firms with capabilities for the coming years.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme, enhanced over four Budgets, will flow a total of $23.5 billion to support 1.9 million jobs over 10 months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Jobs Support Scheme, which I have enhanced over the four Budgets, will flow a total of $23.5 billion to support 1.9 million jobs over 10 months.

sections.label: 100,000 jobseeker opportunities
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo explained about 100,000 opportunities will be created to help local jobseekers take on new jobs, including in emerging and growth areas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As Minister Josephine Teo explained, we will create about 100,000 opportunities to help local jobseekers take on new jobs, including in emerging and growth areas, such as infocomm technologies, financial services and healthcare.

sections.label: Preserving jobs and creating opportunities
sections.summary: Never before has Singapore set out to preserve so many jobs and create so many new opportunities, 100,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Never before in our history have we set out to preserve so many jobs as well as create so many new opportunities – 100,000.

sections.label: Hiring Incentive for mature jobseekers
sections.summary: The Hiring Incentive for eligible mature jobseekers is pegged at 40%, double the rate for younger workers, to help mature workers find new employers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By pegging the Hiring Incentive for eligible mature jobseekers at 40%, which is double the rate for that of younger workers, we are helping more mature workers to find new employers.

sections.label: Banks offering local traineeships
sections.summary: Local and foreign banks are grooming local talent by pledging close to 900 traineeships for local fresh graduates and jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Banks, both local and foreign, are grooming the local talent pipeline, by pledging to offer close to 900 traineeships for local fresh graduates and jobseekers.

sections.label: COVID-19 global economic changes
sections.summary: COVID-19 has triggered a deep cyclical shock and accelerating structural changes, requiring companies worldwide to adjust with speed and agility.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has triggered both a deep cyclical shock and accelerating structural changes in the global economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To thrive, or even to survive, companies all around the world must adjust to these forces with speed and agility.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps launched 2016
sections.summary: From 2016, Industry Transformation Maps were launched to bring stakeholders together to transform industries across 23 sectors and six clusters.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: From 2016, we launched our Industry Transformation Maps to systematically bring together stakeholders to transform our industries, across all 23 sectors and six industry clusters.

sections.label: Forefront Medical pivots to diagnostics
sections.summary: Forefront Medical pivoted into diagnostics by acquiring capabilities in reagent manufacturing for COVID-19 test kits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Forefront Medical also managed to pivot into the diagnostics space by acquiring capabilities in reagent manufacturing for COVID-19 test kits.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget support for firms
sections.summary: The Fortitude Budget cushions firms against cashflow, cost and credit challenges and helps accelerate digital transformation and build capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our Fortitude Budget not only cushions firms to tide over immediate cashflow, cost and credit challenges that Members, including Mr Darryl David and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah spoke about, but also helps accelerate digital transformation and build capabilities to emerge stronger when the recovery comes.

sections.label: MAS study on Budgets
sections.summary: An MAS study estimates the four Budgets help the economy avert an average output loss of five percentage points, or $23.4 billion per year, over 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Based on a recent study by MAS, our four Budgets are estimated to help our economy avert an average output loss of five percentage points, or $23.4 billion per year, over 2020 and 2021.

sections.label: Fortitude Budget Contingencies Funds
sections.summary: Mr Liang Eng Hwa highlighted that the Fortitude Budget sets aside an additional $13 billion in the Contingencies Funds.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, in opening the debate, highlighted a distinctive feature of the Fortitude Budget – that we are setting aside an additional $13 billion in the Contingencies Funds.

sections.label: Yearly Contingencies Funds amount
sections.summary: Each year, $3 billion is in the Contingencies Funds to meet urgent and unforeseen needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Each year, we have $3 billion in the Contingencies Funds to meet urgent and unforeseen needs.

sections.label: President's concurrence for drawdown
sections.summary: The Government will need to seek the President's concurrence for drawing down the Contingencies Funds.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, the Government will need to seek President's concurrence for drawing down the Contingencies Funds.

sections.label: COVID-19 packages and reserves
sections.summary: Three months into FY2020, the accumulated surplus was used up, with COVID-19 packages of nearly $100 billion, over half funded from reserves, against a yearly budget of about $80 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Yet, it took us just three months into FY2020 to use up the accumulated surplus that we had built up over the current term of Government; since the start of this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, mounting COVID-19 packages amounting to nearly $100 billion, of which more than half is funded from the reserves is not a trivial matter, especially when our yearly budget is about $80 billion.

sections.label: Restoring Past Reserves
sections.summary: Ms Foo Mee Har, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Mohd Irshad asked about restoring the $52 billion drawn from Past Reserves; there is no legal or constitutional obligation to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Mohd Irshad asked if we would restore the $52 billion drawn from our Past Reserves, and how long that would take.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: There is no legal or constitutional obligation for the Government to do so.

sections.label: No V-shaped recovery, $52 billion
sections.summary: The passage states there will likely not be a V-shaped recovery, unlike past crises, and that $52 billion is being tapped.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: What we do know is that there will likely not be a V-shaped recovery, unlike in past crises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And the amount that we are tapping on is $52 billion.

sections.label: MAS, Temasek, GIC reserves disclosure
sections.summary: MAS and Temasek invested reserves are public information, but the amount invested by GIC is not disclosed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As Mr Vikram Nair has noted, the size of the reserves invested by MAS and Temasek is public information.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But the amount invested by GIC is not disclosed.

sections.label: Borrowing more at lower interest rates
sections.summary: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether lower interest rates should be used to borrow more to fund expenditure.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked if we should take advantage of the lower interest rates now, to borrow more to fund expenditure.

sections.label: Guarantee for Changi East borrowing
sections.summary: As announced in Budget 2019, the Government will guarantee Changi Airport Group's borrowing to fund Changi East development, including Terminal 5.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, as announced in Budget 2019, the Government will guarantee the borrowing by Changi Airport Group to fund the development of Changi East, including Terminal 5.

sections.label: GST increase timing and Assurance Package
sections.summary: The GST rate increase will not take effect in 2021 but is still needed by 2025, with $6 billion set aside for the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the Unity Budget, I announced that the GST rate increase will not take effect in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: However, we will not be able to put off the increase indefinitely, and this will still be needed by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Six billion dollars in funds have already been set aside during the Unity Budget for the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is sufficient to offset at least five years' worth of additional GST expenses for the majority of households, and more for lower income ones.

sections.label: COVID-19 household benefits during pandemic
sections.summary: During COVID-19, 60% of households can receive additional benefits averaging 12% of household income, double that of the Global Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: During this COVID-19 period, 60% of households can receive additional benefits equivalent to 12% of household income on average.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These benefits include cash assistance from the Temporary Relief Fund, COVID-19 Support Grant and Workfare Special Payment, among others.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is a significant sum – double that given out during the Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: Second phase reopening by June
sections.summary: If everyone is socially responsible, Singapore may enter the second phase of reopening by end of June.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: If everyone is socially responsible, it is possible that by the end of June, we will be able to enter the second phase of reopening.

sections.label: Saving businesses and protecting workers
sections.summary: Government will create jobs, training and cash grants, and help companies cut costs and retain workers to protect livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Only by saving viable businesses can we protect every worker and their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government will spare no efforts to create jobs and training opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The newly established National Jobs Council is also committed to help jobless Singaporeans return to the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will also help companies reduce cost and retain their workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also provide cash grants to Singaporeans, especially to help middle to lower income families manage living expenses, to take care of Singaporeans in need as far as possible.

sections.label: National reserves and no debt
sections.summary: Accumulated national reserves let Singapore respond decisively to the crisis without taking on debt.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are able to accumulate national reserves through the years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Thus, we have been able to respond decisively to the crisis without taking on debt.

sections.label: Past crises Singaporeans experienced
sections.summary: Singaporeans experienced the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis, 2001 dot-com bust, 2003 SARS and 2008 Global Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In recent times, Singaporeans experienced the Asian Financial Crisis in 1997, the dot-com bust in 2001, SARS in 2003 and the Global Financial Crisis in 2008.

sections.label: Reserves, social reserves, unity
sections.summary: Founding generation left a sizeable Reserve and strong social reserves, and Singapore fights from unity, resilience, solidarity and fortitude.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our founding generation left us a legacy of a sizeable Reserve, which we must continue to treasure and build on.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have strong social reserves, supported by mutual trust, close partnerships, strong values and a sense of mutual responsibility and support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But more importantly, we are fighting this battle from a position of Unity, Resilience, Solidarity and Fortitude.

sections.label: Reserves information and rental waiver question
sections.summary: A Member seeks confirmation that the Government gave the President Reserves information and asks about waiving six months' rent for rental flats.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will emerge stronger as an economy, as a society, and as one united, resilient and determined people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I just want to reconfirm that what I have heard from the Deputy Prime Minister is correct with regard to the question that I have asked – whether the Government has provided the President with the information on the amount that we have in the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, am I right to say – and I just want to confirm with the Deputy Prime Minister – that the answer given by him is, yes, the Government did provide this information?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Member can go back to the transcript of the Hansard and the recording of this session.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But, by the way, I should add that, as I have said – and I hope the Member has heard it – the information is public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Could I ask Deputy Prime Minister Heng if he could address the question in my speech about asking if he would consider waiving six months' rent for all households residing in rental flats except for those whose rental is already covered under the ComCare scheme?
